<h1 id="management-api">Management API v3</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

Configure and manage your Adyen company and merchant accounts, stores, and payment terminals.
## Authentication
Each request to the Management API must be signed with an API key. [Generate your API key](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#generate-api-key) in the Customer Area and then set this key to the `X-API-Key` header value.

To access the live endpoints, you need to generate a new API key in your live Customer Area.
## Versioning

Management API handles versioning as part of the endpoint URL. For example, to send a request to this version of the `/companies/{companyId}/webhooks` endpoint, use:

```text
https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/{companyId}/webhooks
```

## Going live

To access the live endpoints, you need an API key from your live Customer Area. Use this API key to make requests to:

```text
https://management-live.adyen.com/v3
```

## Release notes
Have a look at the [release notes](https://docs.adyen.com/release-notes/management-api) to find out what changed in this version!

Base URLs:

* <a href="https://management-test.adyen.com/v3">https://management-test.adyen.com/v3</a>

<a href="https://www.adyen.com/legal/terms-and-conditions">Terms of service</a>
Web: <a href="https://github.com/Adyen/adyen-openapi">Adyen Developer Experience team</a> 

# Authentication

* API Key (ApiKeyAuth)
    - Parameter Name: **X-API-Key**, in: header.

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: basic

<h1 id="management-api-account---company-level">Account - company level</h1>

## Get a list of company accounts

<a id="opIdget-companies"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /companies`

Returns the list of company accounts that your API credential has access to. The list is grouped into pages as defined by the query parameters.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):

* Management API—Account read

<h3 id="get-a-list-of-company-accounts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pageNumber|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of the page to fetch.|
|pageSize|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of items to have on a page, maximum 100. The default is 10 items on a page.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "_links": {
    "first": {
      "href": "https://management-test.adyen.com/v1/companies?pageNumber=1&pageSize=10"
```

## Get a company account

<a id="opIdget-companies-companyId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /companies/{companyId}`

Returns the company account specified in the path. Your API credential must have access to the company account. 

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Account read

<h3 id="get-a-company-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|companyId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the company account.|

## Get a list of merchant accounts

<a id="opIdget-companies-companyId-merchants"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/string/merchants \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /companies/{companyId}/merchants`

Returns the list of merchant accounts under the company account specified in the path. The list only includes merchant accounts that your API credential has access to. The list is grouped into pages as defined by the query parameters. 

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Account read

<h3 id="get-a-list-of-merchant-accounts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|companyId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the company account.|
|pageNumber|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of the page to fetch.|
|pageSize|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of items to have on a page, maximum 100. The default is 10 items on a page.|

<h1 id="management-api-account---merchant-level">Account - merchant level</h1>

## Get a list of merchant accounts

<a id="opIdget-merchants"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /merchants`

Returns the list of merchant accounts that your API credential has access to. The list is grouped into pages as defined by the query parameters. 

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Account read

<h3 id="get-a-list-of-merchant-accounts-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pageNumber|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of the page to fetch.|
|pageSize|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of items to have on a page, maximum 100. The default is 10 items on a page.|

## Create a merchant account

<a id="opIdpost-merchants"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "companyId": "YOUR_COMPANY_ACCOUNT",
    "legalEntityId": "YOUR_LEGAL_ENTITY_ID",
    "businessLineId": "YOUR_BUSINESS_LINE_ID",
    "description": "YOUR_DESCRIPTION",
    "reference": "YOUR_OWN_REFERENCE"
  }'
```

`POST /merchants`

Creates a merchant account for the company account specified in the request.

Use this endpoint if your integration requires it, such as Adyen for Platforms Manage. Your Adyen contact will set up your access.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Accounts read and write

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "companyId": "YOUR_COMPANY_ACCOUNT",
  "legalEntityId": "YOUR_LEGAL_ENTITY_ID",
  "businessLineId": "YOUR_BUSINESS_LINE_ID",
  "description": "YOUR_DESCRIPTION",
  "reference": "YOUR_OWN_REFERENCE"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-merchant-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateMerchantRequest](#schemacreatemerchantrequest)|false|none|
|» businessLineId|body|string|false|The unique identifier of the [business line](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/#/legalentity/latest/post/businessLines). Required for an Adyen for Platforms Manage integration.|
|» companyId|body|string|true|The unique identifier of the company account.|
|» description|body|string|false|Your description for the merchant account, maximum 300 characters.|
|» legalEntityId|body|string|false|The unique identifier of the [legal entity](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/#/legalentity/latest/post/legalEntities). Required for an Adyen for Platforms Manage integration.|
|» pricingPlan|body|string|false|Sets the pricing plan for the merchant account. Required for an Adyen for Platforms Manage integration. Your Adyen contact will provide the values that you can use.|
|» reference|body|string|false|Your reference for the merchant account. To make this reference the unique identifier of the merchant account, your Adyen contact can set up a template on your company account. The template can have 6 to 255 characters with upper- and lower-case letters, underscores, and numbers. When your company account has a template, then the `reference` is required and must be unique within the company account.|
|» salesChannels|body|[string]|false|List of sales channels that the merchant will process payments with|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "companyId": "YOUR_COMPANY_ACCOUNT",
  "legalEntityId": "YOUR_LEGAL_ENTITY_ID",
  "businessLineId": "YOUR_BUSINESS_LINE_ID",
  "description": "YOUR_DESCRIPTION",
  "reference": "YOUR_OWN_REFERENCE",
  "id": "YOUR_OWN_REFERENCE"
}
```

## Get a merchant account

<a id="opIdget-merchants-merchantId"></a>

```bash

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /merchants/{merchantId}`

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):

## Request to activate a merchant account

<a id="opIdpost-merchants-merchantId-activate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/activate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /merchants/{merchantId}/activate`

Sends a request to activate the merchant account identified in the path.

You get the result of the activation asynchronously through a [`merchant.updated`](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/ManagementNotification/latest/post/merchant.updated) webhook. Once the merchant account is activated, you can start using it to accept payments and payouts.

Use this endpoint if your integration requires it, such as Adyen for Platforms Manage. Your Adyen contact will set up your access.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Accounts read and write

<h3 id="request-to-activate-a-merchant-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|

## Get a list of stores

<a id="opIdget-merchants-merchantId-stores"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/stores \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /merchants/{merchantId}/stores`

Returns a list of stores for the merchant account identified in the path. The list is grouped into pages as defined by the query parameters.

To make this request, your API credential must have one of the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Stores read
* Management API—Stores read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

<h3 id="get-a-list-of-stores-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|
|pageNumber|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of the page to fetch.|
|pageSize|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of items to have on a page, maximum 100. The default is 10 items on a page.|
|reference|query|string|false|The reference of the store.|

## Create a store

<a id="opIdpost-merchants-merchantId-stores"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/stores \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "City centre store",
    "shopperStatement": "Springfield Shop",
    "phoneNumber": "13123456789",
    "reference": "Spring_store_2",
    "address": {
      "country": "US",
      "line1": "200 Main Street",
      "line2": "Building 5A",
      "line3": "Suite 3",
      "city": "Springfield",
      "stateOrProvince": "NY",
      "postalCode": "20250"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /merchants/{merchantId}/stores`

Creates a store for the merchant account identified in the path.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Stores read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "City centre store",
  "shopperStatement": "Springfield Shop",
  "phoneNumber": "13123456789",
  "reference": "Spring_store_2",
  "address": {
    "country": "US",
    "line1": "200 Main Street",
    "line2": "Building 5A",
    "line3": "Suite 3",
    "city": "Springfield",
    "stateOrProvince": "NY",
    "postalCode": "20250"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-store-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|
|body|body|[StoreCreationRequest](#schemastorecreationrequest)|false|none|
|» address|body|[StoreLocation](#schemastorelocation)|true|The address of the store.|
|» businessLineIds|body|[string]|false|The unique identifiers of the [business lines](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/legalentity/latest/post/businessLines#responses-200-id) that the store is associated with.<br>If not specified, the business line of the merchant account is used. Required when there are multiple business lines under the merchant account.|
|» description|body|string|true|Your description of the store.|
|» externalReferenceId|body|string|false|The unique identifier of the store, used by certain payment methods and tax authorities.<br><br>Required for CNPJ in Brazil, in the format 00.000.000/0000-00 separated by dots, slashes, hyphens, or without separators.<br><br>Optional for SIRET in France, up to 14 digits.<br><br>Optional for Zip in Australia, up to 50 digits.<br><br>|
|» localizedInformation|body|[LocalizedInformation](#schemalocalizedinformation)|false|Localized information about the store.|
|» phoneNumber|body|string|true|The phone number of the store, including '+' and country code in the [E.164](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E.164) format. If passed in a different format, we convert and validate the phone number against E.164. |
|» reference|body|string|false|Your reference to recognize the store by. Also known as the store code.<br> Allowed characters: lowercase and uppercase letters without diacritics, numbers 0 through 9, hyphen (-), and underscore (_).<br><br>If you do not provide a reference in your POST request, it is populated with the Adyen-generated [id](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/Management/latest/post/stores#responses-200-id).|
|» shopperStatement|body|string|true|The store name to be shown on the shopper's bank or credit card statement and on the shopper receipt.<br>Maximum length: 22 characters; can't be all numbers.|
|» splitConfiguration|body|[StoreSplitConfiguration](#schemastoresplitconfiguration)|false|Rules for Adyen for Platforms merchants to split the transaction amount and fees.|
|» subMerchantData|body|[SubMerchantData](#schemasubmerchantdata)|false|The sub-merchant data relevant for registered payment facilitators transacting on standalone terminals.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "YOUR_STORE_ID",
  "address": {
    "country": "US",
    "line1": "200 Main Street",
    "line2": "Building 5A",
    "line3": "Suite 3",
    "city": "Springfield",
    "stateOrProvince": "NY",
    "postalCode": "20250"
  },
  "description": "City centre store",
  "merchantId": "YOUR_MERCHANT_ACCOUNT_ID",
  "shopperStatement": "Springfield Shop",

  "status": "active",
  "_links": {

    }
  }
}
```

```bash
      "line2": "Heartland Building",
      "line3": "",
      "postalCode": "20251"
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /merchants/{merchantId}/stores/{storeId}`

Updates the store identified in the path. You can only update some store parameters.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Stores read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "address": {
    "line1": "1776 West Pinewood Avenue",
    "line2": "Heartland Building",
    "line3": "",
    "postalCode": "20251"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-store-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|
|storeId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the store.|
|body|body|[UpdateStoreRequest](#schemaupdatestorerequest)|false|none|
|» address|body|[UpdatableAddress](#schemaupdatableaddress)|false|The address of the store. It is not possible to update the country of the store.|
|» businessLineIds|body|[string]|false|The unique identifiers of the [business lines](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/#/legalentity/latest/post/businessLines__resParam_id) that the store is associated with.|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the store.|
|» externalReferenceId|body|string|false|The unique identifier of the store, used by certain payment methods and tax authorities.<br><br>Required for CNPJ in Brazil, in the format 00.000.000/0000-00 separated by dots, slashes, hyphens, or without separators.<br><br>Optional for SIRET in France, up to 14 digits.<br><br>Optional for Zip in Australia, up to 50 digits.<br><br>|
|» phoneNumber|body|string|false|The phone number of the store, including '+' and country code in the [E.164](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E.164) format. If passed in a different format, we convert and validate the phone number against E.164. |
|» splitConfiguration|body|[StoreSplitConfiguration](#schemastoresplitconfiguration)|false|Rules for Adyen for Platforms merchants to split the transaction amount and fees.|
|» status|body|string|false|The status of the store. Possible values are:<br><br>- **active**: This value is assigned automatically when a store is created. <br>- **inactive**: The maximum [transaction limits and number of Store-and-Forward transactions](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/determine-account-structure/configure-features#payment-features) for the store are set to 0. This blocks new transactions, but captures are still possible.<br>- **closed**: The terminals of the store are reassigned to the merchant inventory, so they can't process payments.<br><br>You can change the status from **active** to **inactive**, and from **inactive** to **active** or **closed**. <br>Once **closed**, a store can't be reopened.|
|» subMerchantData|body|[SubMerchantData](#schemasubmerchantdata)|false|The sub-merchant data relevant for registered payment facilitators transacting on standalone terminals.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» status|active|
|» status|closed|
|» status|inactive|

## Get a list of stores

<a id="opIdget-stores"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/stores \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /stores`

Returns a list of stores. The list is grouped into pages as defined by the query parameters.

To make this request, your API credential must have one of the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Stores read
* Management API—Stores read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

<h3 id="get-a-list-of-stores-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pageNumber|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of the page to fetch.|
|pageSize|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of items to have on a page, maximum 100. The default is 10 items on a page.|
|reference|query|string|false|The reference of the store.|
|merchantId|query|string|false|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|

## Create a store

<a id="opIdpost-stores"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/stores \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "merchantId": "YOUR_MERCHANT_ACCOUNT_ID",
    "description": "City centre store",
    "shopperStatement": "Springfield Shop",
    "phoneNumber": "+13123456789",
    "reference": "Spring_store_2",
    "address": {
      "country": "US",
      "line1": "200 Main Street",
      "line2": "Building 5A",
      "line3": "Suite 3",
      "city": "Springfield",
      "stateOrProvince": "NY",
      "postalCode": "20250"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /stores`

Creates a store for the merchant account specified in the request.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Stores read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "merchantId": "YOUR_MERCHANT_ACCOUNT_ID",
  "description": "City centre store",
  "shopperStatement": "Springfield Shop",
  "phoneNumber": "+13123456789",
  "reference": "Spring_store_2",
  "address": {
    "country": "US",
    "line1": "200 Main Street",
    "line2": "Building 5A",
    "line3": "Suite 3",
    "city": "Springfield",
    "stateOrProvince": "NY",
    "postalCode": "20250"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-store-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[StoreCreationWithMerchantCodeRequest](#schemastorecreationwithmerchantcoderequest)|false|none|
|» address|body|[StoreLocation](#schemastorelocation)|true|The address of the store.|
|» businessLineIds|body|[string]|false|The unique identifiers of the [business lines](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/legalentity/latest/post/businessLines#responses-200-id) that the store is associated with.<br>If not specified, the business line of the merchant account is used. Required when there are multiple business lines under the merchant account.|
|» description|body|string|true|Your description of the store.|
|» externalReferenceId|body|string|false|The unique identifier of the store, used by certain payment methods and tax authorities.<br><br>Required for CNPJ in Brazil, in the format 00.000.000/0000-00 separated by dots, slashes, hyphens, or without separators.<br><br>Optional for SIRET in France, up to 14 digits.<br><br>Optional for Zip in Australia, up to 50 digits.<br><br>|
|» localizedInformation|body|[LocalizedInformation](#schemalocalizedinformation)|false|Localized information about the store.|
|» merchantId|body|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account that the store belongs to.|
|» phoneNumber|body|string|true|The phone number of the store, including '+' and country code in the [E.164](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E.164) format. If passed in a different format, we convert and validate the phone number against E.164. |
|» reference|body|string|false|Your reference to recognize the store by. Also known as the store code.<br> Allowed characters: lowercase and uppercase letters without diacritics, numbers 0 through 9, hyphen (-), and underscore (_).<br><br>If you do not provide a reference in your POST request, it is populated with the Adyen-generated [id](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/Management/latest/post/stores#responses-200-id).|
|» shopperStatement|body|string|true|The store name to be shown on the shopper's bank or credit card statement and on the shopper receipt.<br>Maximum length: 22 characters; can't be all numbers.|
|» splitConfiguration|body|[StoreSplitConfiguration](#schemastoresplitconfiguration)|false|Rules for Adyen for Platforms merchants to split the transaction amount and fees.|
|» subMerchantData|body|[SubMerchantData](#schemasubmerchantdata)|false|The sub-merchant data relevant for registered payment facilitators transacting on standalone terminals.|

> Example responses

## Update a store

<a id="opIdpatch-stores-storeId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/stores/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "address": {
      "line1": "1776 West Pinewood Avenue",
      "line2": "Heartland Building",
      "line3": "",
      "postalCode": "20251"
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /stores/{storeId}`

Updates the store identified in the path.
You can only update some store parameters.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Stores read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "address": {
    "line1": "1776 West Pinewood Avenue",
    "line2": "Heartland Building",
    "line3": "",
    "postalCode": "20251"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-store-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|storeId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the store.|
|body|body|[UpdateStoreRequest](#schemaupdatestorerequest)|false|none|
|» address|body|[UpdatableAddress](#schemaupdatableaddress)|false|The address of the store. It is not possible to update the country of the store.|
|» businessLineIds|body|[string]|false|The unique identifiers of the [business lines](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/#/legalentity/latest/post/businessLines__resParam_id) that the store is associated with.|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the store.|
|» externalReferenceId|body|string|false|The unique identifier of the store, used by certain payment methods and tax authorities.<br><br>Required for CNPJ in Brazil, in the format 00.000.000/0000-00 separated by dots, slashes, hyphens, or without separators.<br><br>Optional for SIRET in France, up to 14 digits.<br><br>Optional for Zip in Australia, up to 50 digits.<br><br>|
|» phoneNumber|body|string|false|The phone number of the store, including '+' and country code in the [E.164](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E.164) format. If passed in a different format, we convert and validate the phone number against E.164. |
|» splitConfiguration|body|[StoreSplitConfiguration](#schemastoresplitconfiguration)|false|Rules for Adyen for Platforms merchants to split the transaction amount and fees.|
|» status|body|string|false|The status of the store. Possible values are:<br><br>- **active**: This value is assigned automatically when a store is created. <br>- **inactive**: The maximum [transaction limits and number of Store-and-Forward transactions](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/determine-account-structure/configure-features#payment-features) for the store are set to 0. This blocks new transactions, but captures are still possible.<br>- **closed**: The terminals of the store are reassigned to the merchant inventory, so they can't process payments.<br><br>You can change the status from **active** to **inactive**, and from **inactive** to **active** or **closed**. <br>Once **closed**, a store can't be reopened.|
|» subMerchantData|body|[SubMerchantData](#schemasubmerchantdata)|false|The sub-merchant data relevant for registered payment facilitators transacting on standalone terminals.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» status|active|
|» status|closed|
|» status|inactive|

## Add a payout setting

<a id="opIdpost-merchants-merchantId-payoutSettings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/payoutSettings \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "enabled": true,
    "enabledFromDate": "string",
    "transferInstrumentId": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /merchants/{merchantId}/payoutSettings`

Sends a request to add a payout setting for the merchant account specified in the path. A payout setting links the merchant account to the [transfer instrument](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/#/legalentity/latest/post/transferInstruments) that contains the details of the payout bank account. Adyen verifies the bank account before allowing and enabling the payout setting.

If you're accepting payments in multiple currencies, you may add multiple payout settings for the merchant account.

Use this endpoint if your integration requires it, such as Adyen for Platforms Manage. Your Adyen contact will set up your access.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):

* Management API—Payout account settings read and write

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "enabledFromDate": "string",
  "transferInstrumentId": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="add-a-payout-setting-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|
|body|body|[PayoutSettingsRequest](#schemapayoutsettingsrequest)|false|none|
|» enabled|body|boolean|false|Indicates if payouts to this bank account are enabled. Default: **true**.<br><br>To receive payouts into this bank account, both `enabled` and `allowed` must be **true**.|
|» enabledFromDate|body|string|false|The date when Adyen starts paying out to this bank account.<br><br>Format: [ISO 8601](https://www.w3.org/TR/NOTE-datetime), for example, **2019-11-23T12:25:28Z** or **2020-05-27T20:25:28+08:00**.<br><br>If not specified, the `enabled` field indicates if payouts are enabled for this bank account.<br><br>If a date is specified and:<br><br>* `enabled`: **true**, payouts are enabled starting the specified date.<br>* `enabled`: **false**, payouts are disabled until the specified date. On the specified date, `enabled` changes to **true** and this field is reset to **null**.|
|» transferInstrumentId|body|string|true|The unique identifier of the [transfer instrument](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/#/legalentity/latest/post/transferInstruments) that contains the details of the bank account.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "allowed": true,
  "enabled": true,
  "enabledFromDate": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "priority": "first",
  "transferInstrumentId": "string",
  "verificationStatus": "invalid"
}
```

> 400 Response

## Update a payout setting

<a id="opIdpatch-merchants-merchantId-payoutSettings-payoutSettingsId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/payoutSettings/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "enabled": true
  }'
```

`PATCH /merchants/{merchantId}/payoutSettings/{payoutSettingsId}`

Updates the payout setting identified in the path. You can enable or disable the payout setting.

Use this endpoint if your integration requires it, such as Adyen for Platforms Manage. Your Adyen contact will set up your access.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):

* Management API—Payout account settings read and write

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "enabled": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-payout-setting-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|
|payoutSettingsId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the payout setting.|
|body|body|[UpdatePayoutSettingsRequest](#schemaupdatepayoutsettingsrequest)|false|none|
|» enabled|body|boolean|false|Indicates if payouts to this bank account are enabled. Default: **true**.<br><br>To receive payouts into this bank account, both `enabled` and `allowed` must be **true**.|

## Create a new user

<a id="opIdpost-companies-companyId-users"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/string/users \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "name": {
      "firstName": "John",
      "lastName": "Smith"
    },
    "username": "johnsmith",
    "email": "john.smith@example.com",
    "loginMethod": "Email",
    "timeZoneCode": "Europe/Amsterdam",
    "roles": [
      "Merchant standard role",
      "Merchant admin"
    ],
    "associatedMerchantAccounts": [
      "YOUR_MERCHANT_ACCOUNT"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /companies/{companyId}/users`

Creates the user for the `companyId` identified in the path.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Users read and write


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": {
    "firstName": "John",
    "lastName": "Smith"
  },
  "username": "johnsmith",
  "email": "john.smith@example.com",
  "loginMethod": "Email",
  "timeZoneCode": "Europe/Amsterdam",
  "roles": [
    "Merchant standard role",
    "Merchant admin"
  ],
  "associatedMerchantAccounts": [

  ]
}
```

## Create a new user

<a id="opIdpost-merchants-merchantId-users"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/users \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "name": {
      "firstName": "John",
      "lastName": "Smith"
    },
    "username": "johnsmith",
    "email": "john.smith@example.com",
    "loginMethod": "Email",
    "timeZoneCode": "Europe/Amsterdam",
    "roles": [
      "Merchant standard role"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /merchants/{merchantId}/users`

Creates a user for the `merchantId` specified in the path.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Users read and write


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": {
    "firstName": "John",
    "lastName": "Smith"
  },
  "username": "johnsmith",
  "email": "john.smith@example.com",
  "loginMethod": "Email",
  "timeZoneCode": "Europe/Amsterdam",
  "roles": [
    "Merchant standard role"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-user-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the merchant.|
|body|body|[CreateMerchantUserRequest](#schemacreatemerchantuserrequest)|false|none|
|» accountGroups|body|[string]|false|The list of [account groups](https://docs.adyen.com/account/account-structure#account-groups) associated with this user.|
|» email|body|string|true|The email address of the user.|
|» loginMethod|body|string|false|The requested login method for the user. To use SSO, you must already have SSO configured with Adyen before creating the user.<br><br>Possible values: **Email** or **SSO** |
|» name|body|[Name](#schemaname)|true|The user's full name.<br><br>Allowed length: 1—80 characters.|
|» roles|body|[string]|false|The list of [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/account/user-roles) for this user.|
|» timeZoneCode|body|string|false|The [tz database name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tz_database_time_zones) of the time zone of the user. For example, **Europe/Amsterdam**.|
|» username|body|string|true|The user's email address that will be their username. Must be the same as the one in the `email` field.|

## Add allowed origin

<a id="opIdpost-me-allowedOrigins"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/me/allowedOrigins \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "_links": {
      "self": {
        "href": "string"
      }
    },
    "domain": "https://adyen.com",
    "id": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /me/allowedOrigins`

Adds an allowed origin to the list of [allowed origins](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/client-side-authentication#allowed-origins) of your API credential.
The API key from the request is used to identify the [API credential](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials).

You can make this request with any of the Management API roles.

```json
{
  "_links": {
    "self": {
      "href": "string"
    }
  },
  "domain": "https://adyen.com",
  "id": "string"
}
```

|body|body|[CreateAllowedOriginRequest](#schemacreateallowedoriginrequest)|false|none|

|» domain|body|string|true|Domain of the allowed origin.|
|» id|body|string|false|Unique identifier of the allowed origin.|

<h1 id="management-api-api-credentials---company-level">API credentials - company level</h1>

## Get a list of API credentials

<a id="opIdget-companies-companyId-apiCredentials"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/string/apiCredentials \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /companies/{companyId}/apiCredentials`

Returns the list of [API credentials](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials) for the company account. The list is grouped into pages as defined by the query parameters.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—API credentials read and write

<h3 id="get-a-list-of-api-credentials-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|companyId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the company account.|
|pageNumber|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of the page to fetch.|
|pageSize|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of items to have on a page, maximum 100. The default is 10 items on a page.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "_links": {
    "first": {
      "href": "https://management-test.adyen.com/v1/companies/YOUR_COMPANY_ACCOUNT/apiCredentials?pageNumber=1&pageSize=10"
    },
    "last": {
      "href": "https://management-test.adyen.com/v1/companies/YOUR_COMPANY_ACCOUNT/apiCredentials?pageNumber=3&pageSize=10"
    },

      "href": "https://management-test.adyen.com/v1/companies/YOUR_COMPANY_ACCOUNT/apiCredentials?pageNumber=2&pageSize=10"
    },
    "self": {
      "href": "https://management-test.adyen.com/v1/companies/YOUR_COMPANY_ACCOUNT/apiCredentials?pageNumber=1&pageSize=10"
    }
  },
```

</aside>

## Create an API credential.

<a id="opIdpost-companies-companyId-apiCredentials"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/string/apiCredentials \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "roles": [
      "Checkout webservice role"
    ],
    "allowedOrigins": [
      "https://www.mystore.com"
    ],
    "associatedMerchantAccounts": [
      "YOUR_MERCHANT_ACCOUNT_AU",
      "YOUR_MERCHANT_ACCOUNT_EU",
      "YOUR_MERCHANT_ACCOUNT_US"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /companies/{companyId}/apiCredentials`

Creates an [API credential](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials) for the company account identified in the path. In the request, you can specify which merchant accounts the new API credential will have access to, as well as its roles and allowed origins.

The response includes several types of authentication details:
* [API key](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-authentication#api-key-authentication): used for API request authentication.
* [Client key](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/client-side-authentication#how-it-works): public key used for client-side authentication.
* [Username and password](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-authentication#using-basic-authentication): used for basic authentication.

> Make sure you store the API key securely in your system. You won't be able to retrieve it later.

If your API key is lost or compromised, you need to [generate a new API key](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/#/ManagementService/v1/post/companies/{companyId}/apiCredentials/{apiCredentialId}/generateApiKey).

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—API credentials read and write

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "roles": [
    "Checkout webservice role"
  ],
  "allowedOrigins": [
    "https://www.mystore.com"
  ],
  "associatedMerchantAccounts": [
    "YOUR_MERCHANT_ACCOUNT_AU",
    "YOUR_MERCHANT_ACCOUNT_EU",
    "YOUR_MERCHANT_ACCOUNT_US"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-api-credential-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|companyId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the company account.|
|body|body|[CreateCompanyApiCredentialRequest](#schemacreatecompanyapicredentialrequest)|false|none|
|» allowedOrigins|body|[string]|false|List of [allowed origins](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/client-side-authentication#allowed-origins) for the new API credential.|
|» associatedMerchantAccounts|body|[string]|false|List of merchant accounts that the API credential has access to.|
|» description|body|string|false|Description of the API credential.|
|» roles|body|[string]|false|List of [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#roles-1) for the API credential. Only roles assigned to 'ws@Company.<CompanyName>' can be assigned to other API credentials.|

## Update an API credential.

<a id="opIdpatch-companies-companyId-apiCredentials-apiCredentialId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/string/apiCredentials/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "active": true
  }'
```

`PATCH /companies/{companyId}/apiCredentials/{apiCredentialId}`

Changes the API credential's roles, merchant account access, or allowed origins. The request has the new values for the fields you want to change. The response contains the full updated API credential, including the new values from the request. 

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—API credentials read and write

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "active": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-api-credential-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|companyId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the company account.|
|apiCredentialId|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the API credential.|
|body|body|[UpdateCompanyApiCredentialRequest](#schemaupdatecompanyapicredentialrequest)|false|none|
|» active|body|boolean|false|Indicates if the API credential is enabled.|
|» allowedOrigins|body|[string]|false|The new list of [allowed origins](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/client-side-authentication#allowed-origins) for the API credential.|
|» associatedMerchantAccounts|body|[string]|false|List of merchant accounts that the API credential has access to.|
|» description|body|string|false|Description of the API credential.|
|» roles|body|[string]|false|List of [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#roles-1) for the API credential. Only roles assigned to 'ws@Company.<CompanyName>' can be assigned to other API credentials.|
|» subjectDN|body|string|false|The subject DN of the certificate issued by Adyen.|

## Get a list of API credentials

<a id="opIdget-merchants-merchantId-apiCredentials"></a>

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/apiCredentials \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /merchants/{merchantId}/apiCredentials`

Returns the list of [API credentials](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials) for the merchant account. The list is grouped into pages as defined by the query parameters.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—API credentials read and write

|merchantId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|
|pageNumber|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of the page to fetch.|
|pageSize|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of items to have on a page, maximum 100. The default is 10 items on a page.|

## Create an API credential

<a id="opIdpost-merchants-merchantId-apiCredentials"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/apiCredentials \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "roles": [
      "Checkout webservice role"
    ],
    "allowedOrigins": [
      "https://www.mystore.com"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /merchants/{merchantId}/apiCredentials`

Creates an [API credential](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials) for the company account identified in the path. In the request, you can specify the roles and allowed origins for the new API credential.

The response includes the:
* [API key](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-authentication#api-key-authentication): used for API request authentication.
* [Client key](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/client-side-authentication#how-it-works): public key used for client-side authentication.
* [Username and password](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-authentication#using-basic-authentication): used for basic authentication.

> Make sure you store the API key securely in your system. You won't be able to retrieve it later.

If your API key is lost or compromised, you need to [generate a new API key](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/#/ManagementService/v1/post/merchants/{merchantId}/apiCredentials/{apiCredentialId}/generateApiKey).

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—API credentials read and write

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "roles": [
    "Checkout webservice role"
  ],
  "allowedOrigins": [
    "https://www.mystore.com"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-api-credential-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|
|body|body|[CreateMerchantApiCredentialRequest](#schemacreatemerchantapicredentialrequest)|false|none|
|» allowedOrigins|body|[string]|false|The list of [allowed origins](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/client-side-authentication#allowed-origins) for the new API credential.|
|» description|body|string|false|Description of the API credential.|
|» roles|body|[string]|false|List of [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#roles-1) for the API credential. Only roles assigned to 'ws@Company.<CompanyName>' can be assigned to other API credentials.|

> Example responses

```json
  ],

        }
      }
    }
  ],

    },

    },
```

## Update an API credential

<a id="opIdpatch-merchants-merchantId-apiCredentials-apiCredentialId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/apiCredentials/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "active": true
  }'
```

`PATCH /merchants/{merchantId}/apiCredentials/{apiCredentialId}`

Changes the API credential's roles, or allowed origins. The request has the new values for the fields you want to change. The response contains the full updated API credential, including the new values from the request. 

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—API credentials read and write

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "active": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-api-credential-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|
|apiCredentialId|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the API credential.|
|body|body|[UpdateMerchantApiCredentialRequest](#schemaupdatemerchantapicredentialrequest)|false|none|
|» active|body|boolean|false|Indicates if the API credential is enabled.|
|» allowedOrigins|body|[string]|false|The new list of [allowed origins](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/client-side-authentication#allowed-origins) for the API credential.|
|» description|body|string|false|Description of the API credential.|
|» roles|body|[string]|false|List of [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#roles-1) for the API credential. Only roles assigned to 'ws@Company.<CompanyName>' can be assigned to other API credentials.|
|» subjectDN|body|string|false|The subject DN of the certificate issued by Adyen.|

> Example responses

## Create an allowed origin

<a id="opIdpost-companies-companyId-apiCredentials-apiCredentialId-allowedOrigins"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/string/apiCredentials/string/allowedOrigins \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "domain": "https://www.eu.mystore.com"
  }'
```

`POST /companies/{companyId}/apiCredentials/{apiCredentialId}/allowedOrigins`

Adds a new [allowed origin](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/client-side-authentication#allowed-origins) to the API credential's list of allowed origins.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—API credentials read and write

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "domain": "https://www.eu.mystore.com"
```

## Delete an allowed origin

<a id="opIddelete-merchants-merchantId-apiCredentials-apiCredentialId-allowedOrigins-originId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/apiCredentials/string/allowedOrigins/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /merchants/{merchantId}/apiCredentials/{apiCredentialId}/allowedOrigins/{originId}`

Removes the [allowed origin](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/client-side-authentication#allowed-origins) identified in the path. As soon as an allowed origin is removed, we no longer accept client-side requests from that domain.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—API credentials read and write

<h3 id="delete-an-allowed-origin-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|
|apiCredentialId|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the API credential.|
|originId|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the allowed origin.|

`GET /companies/{companyId}/webhooks`

To make this request, your API credential must have one of the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):

|pageNumber|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of the page to fetch.|
|pageSize|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of items to have on a page, maximum 100. The default is 10 items on a page.|

## Set up a webhook

<a id="opIdpost-companies-companyId-webhooks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/string/webhooks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "standard",
    "url": "YOUR_WEBHOOK_URL",
    "username": "YOUR_USER",
    "password": "YOUR_PASSWORD",
    "active": true,
    "communicationFormat": "soap",
    "acceptsExpiredCertificate": false,
    "acceptsSelfSignedCertificate": true,
    "acceptsUntrustedRootCertificate": true,
    "populateSoapActionHeader": false,
    "filterMerchantAccountType": "includeAccounts",
    "filterMerchantAccounts": [
      "YOUR_MERCHANT_ACCOUNT"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /companies/{companyId}/webhooks`

Subscribe to receive webhook notifications about events related to your company account. You can add basic authentication to make sure the data is secure.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Webhooks read and write

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "standard",
  "url": "YOUR_WEBHOOK_URL",
  "username": "YOUR_USER",
  "password": "YOUR_PASSWORD",
  "active": true,
  "communicationFormat": "soap",
  "acceptsExpiredCertificate": false,
  "acceptsSelfSignedCertificate": true,
  "acceptsUntrustedRootCertificate": true,
  "populateSoapActionHeader": false,
  "filterMerchantAccountType": "includeAccounts",
  "filterMerchantAccounts": [
    "YOUR_MERCHANT_ACCOUNT"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="set-up-a-webhook-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|companyId|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the [company account](https://docs.adyen.com/account/account-structure#company-account).|
|body|body|[CreateCompanyWebhookRequest](#schemacreatecompanywebhookrequest)|false|none|
|» acceptsExpiredCertificate|body|boolean|false|Indicates if expired SSL certificates are accepted. Default value: **false**.|
|» acceptsSelfSignedCertificate|body|boolean|false|Indicates if self-signed SSL certificates are accepted. Default value: **false**.|
|» acceptsUntrustedRootCertificate|body|boolean|false|Indicates if untrusted SSL certificates are accepted. Default value: **false**.|
|» active|body|boolean|true|Indicates if the webhook configuration is active. The field must be **true** for us to send webhooks about events related an account.|
|» additionalSettings|body|[AdditionalSettings](#schemaadditionalsettings)|false|Additional shopper and transaction information to be included in your [standard webhooks](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/webhooks/webhook-types/#event-codes). Find out more about the available [additional settings](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/webhooks/additional-settings).|
|» communicationFormat|body|string|true|Format or protocol for receiving webhooks. Possible values:<br>* **soap**<br>* **http**<br>* **json** |
|» description|body|string|false|Your description for this webhook configuration.|
|» encryptionProtocol|body|string|false|SSL version to access the public webhook URL specified in the `url` field. Possible values:<br>* **TLSv1.3**<br>* **TLSv1.2**<br>* **HTTP** - Only allowed on Test environment.<br><br>If not specified, the webhook will use `sslVersion`: **TLSv1.2**.|
|» filterMerchantAccountType|body|string|true|Shows how merchant accounts are filtered when configuring the webhook. <br><br>Possible values:<br>*  **allAccounts** : Includes all merchant accounts, and does not require specifying `filterMerchantAccounts`.<br>*  **includeAccounts** : The webhook is configured for the merchant accounts listed in `filterMerchantAccounts`.<br>*  **excludeAccounts** : The webhook is not configured for the merchant accounts listed in `filterMerchantAccounts`.<br><br>|
|» filterMerchantAccounts|body|[string]|true|A list of merchant account names that are included or excluded from receiving the webhook. Inclusion or exclusion is based on the value defined for `filterMerchantAccountType`.<br><br>Required if `filterMerchantAccountType` is either:<br>* **includeAccounts**<br>* **excludeAccounts**<br><br>Not needed for `filterMerchantAccountType`: **allAccounts**.|
|» networkType|body|string|false|Network type for Terminal API notification webhooks. Possible values:<br>* **public**<br>* **local**<br><br>Default Value: **public**.|
|» password|body|string|false|Password to access the webhook URL.|
|» populateSoapActionHeader|body|boolean|false|Indicates if the SOAP action header needs to be populated. Default value: **false**.<br><br>Only applies if `communicationFormat`: **soap**.|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of webhook that is being created. Possible values are:<br><br>- **standard**<br>- **account-settings-notification**<br>- **banktransfer-notification**<br>- **boletobancario-notification**<br>- **directdebit-notification**<br>- **ach-notification-of-change-notification**<br>- **direct-debit-notice-of-change-notification**<br>- **pending-notification**<br>- **ideal-notification**<br>- **ideal-pending-notification**<br>- **report-notification**<br>- **rreq-notification**<br>- **terminal-settings**<br>- **terminal-boarding**<br><br>Find out more about [standard webhooks](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/webhooks/webhook-types/#event-codes) and [other types of webhooks](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/webhooks/webhook-types/#other-webhooks).|
|» url|body|string|true|Public URL where webhooks will be sent, for example **https://www.domain.com/webhook-endpoint**.|
|» username|body|string|false|Username to access the webhook URL.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» communicationFormat|http|
|» communicationFormat|json|
|» communicationFormat|soap|
|» encryptionProtocol|HTTP|
|» encryptionProtocol|TLSv1.2|
|» encryptionProtocol|TLSv1.3|
|» filterMerchantAccountType|allAccounts|
|» filterMerchantAccountType|excludeAccounts|
|» filterMerchantAccountType|includeAccounts|
|» networkType|local|
|» networkType|public|

## Update a webhook

<a id="opIdpatch-companies-companyId-webhooks-webhookId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/string/webhooks/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "active": true
  }'
```

`PATCH /companies/{companyId}/webhooks/{webhookId}`

Make changes to the configuration of the webhook identified in the path. The request contains the new values you want to have in the webhook configuration. The response contains the full configuration for the webhook, which includes the new values from the request.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Webhooks read and write

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "active": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-webhook-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|companyId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the company account.|
|webhookId|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the webhook configuration.|
|body|body|[UpdateCompanyWebhookRequest](#schemaupdatecompanywebhookrequest)|false|none|
|» acceptsExpiredCertificate|body|boolean|false|Indicates if expired SSL certificates are accepted. Default value: **false**.|
|» acceptsSelfSignedCertificate|body|boolean|false|Indicates if self-signed SSL certificates are accepted. Default value: **false**.|
|» acceptsUntrustedRootCertificate|body|boolean|false|Indicates if untrusted SSL certificates are accepted. Default value: **false**.|
|» active|body|boolean|false|Indicates if the webhook configuration is active. The field must be **true** for us to send webhooks about events related an account.|
|» additionalSettings|body|[AdditionalSettings](#schemaadditionalsettings)|false|Additional shopper and transaction information to be included in your [standard webhooks](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/webhooks/webhook-types/#event-codes). Find out more about the available [additional settings](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/webhooks/additional-settings).|
|» communicationFormat|body|string|false|Format or protocol for receiving webhooks. Possible values:<br>* **soap**<br>* **http**<br>* **json** |
|» description|body|string|false|Your description for this webhook configuration.|
|» encryptionProtocol|body|string|false|SSL version to access the public webhook URL specified in the `url` field. Possible values:<br>* **TLSv1.3**<br>* **TLSv1.2**<br>* **HTTP** - Only allowed on Test environment.<br><br>If not specified, the webhook will use `sslVersion`: **TLSv1.2**.|
|» filterMerchantAccountType|body|string|false|Shows how merchant accounts are filtered when configuring the webhook. Possible values:<br>* **includeAccounts**: The webhook is configured for the merchant accounts listed in `filterMerchantAccounts`.<br>* **excludeAccounts**: The webhook is not configured for the merchant accounts listed in `filterMerchantAccounts`.<br>* **allAccounts**: Includes all merchant accounts, and does not require specifying `filterMerchantAccounts`.|
|» filterMerchantAccounts|body|[string]|false|A list of merchant account names that are included or excluded from receiving the webhook. Inclusion or exclusion is based on the value defined for `filterMerchantAccountType`.<br><br>Required if `filterMerchantAccountType` is either:<br>* **includeAccounts**<br>* **excludeAccounts**<br><br>Not needed for `filterMerchantAccountType`: **allAccounts**.|
|» networkType|body|string|false|Network type for Terminal API notification webhooks. Possible values:<br>* **public**<br>* **local**<br><br>Default Value: **public**.|
|» password|body|string|false|Password to access the webhook URL.|
|» populateSoapActionHeader|body|boolean|false|Indicates if the SOAP action header needs to be populated. Default value: **false**.<br><br>Only applies if `communicationFormat`: **soap**.|
|» url|body|string|false|Public URL where webhooks will be sent, for example **https://www.domain.com/webhook-endpoint**.|
|» username|body|string|false|Username to access the webhook URL.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» communicationFormat|http|
|» communicationFormat|json|
|» communicationFormat|soap|
|» encryptionProtocol|HTTP|
|» encryptionProtocol|TLSv1.2|
|» encryptionProtocol|TLSv1.3|
|» filterMerchantAccountType|allAccounts|
|» filterMerchantAccountType|excludeAccounts|
|» filterMerchantAccountType|includeAccounts|
|» networkType|local|
|» networkType|public|

## Generate an HMAC key

<a id="opIdpost-companies-companyId-webhooks-webhookId-generateHmac"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/string/webhooks/string/generateHmac \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /companies/{companyId}/webhooks/{webhookId}/generateHmac`

Returns an [HMAC key](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMAC) for the webhook identified in the path. This key allows you to check the integrity and the origin of the notifications you receive.By creating an HMAC key, you start receiving [HMAC-signed notifications](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/webhooks/verify-hmac-signatures#enable-hmac-signatures) from Adyen. Find out more about how to [verify HMAC signatures](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/webhooks/verify-hmac-signatures).

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Webhooks read and write

<h3 id="generate-an-hmac-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|companyId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the company account.|
|webhookId|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the webhook configuration.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

## Test a webhook

<a id="opIdpost-companies-companyId-webhooks-webhookId-test"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/string/webhooks/string/test \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "merchantIds": [
      "YOUR_MERCHANT_ACCOUNT"
    ],
    "types": [
      "AUTHORISATION"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /companies/{companyId}/webhooks/{webhookId}/test`

Sends sample notifications to test if the webhook is set up correctly.

We send sample notifications for maximum 20 of the merchant accounts that the webhook is configured for. If the webhook is configured for more than 20 merchant accounts, use the `merchantIds` array to specify a subset of the merchant accounts for which to send test notifications.

We send four test notifications for each event code you choose. They cover success and failure scenarios for the hard-coded currencies EUR and GBP, regardless of the currencies configured in the merchant accounts. For custom notifications, we only send the specified custom notification.

The response describes the result of the test. The `status` field tells you if the test was successful or not. You can use the other response fields to troubleshoot unsuccessful tests.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Webhooks read and write

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "merchantIds": [
    "YOUR_MERCHANT_ACCOUNT"
  ],
  "types": [
    "AUTHORISATION"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="test-a-webhook-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|companyId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the company account.|
|webhookId|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the webhook configuration.|
|body|body|[TestCompanyWebhookRequest](#schematestcompanywebhookrequest)|false|none|
|» merchantIds|body|[string]|false|List of `merchantId` values for which test webhooks will be sent. The list can have a maximum of 20 `merchantId` values.<br><br>If not specified, we send sample notifications to all the merchant accounts that the webhook is configured for. If this is more than 20 merchant accounts, use this list to specify a subset of the merchant accounts for which to send test notifications.|
|» notification|body|[CustomNotification](#schemacustomnotification)|false|Custom test notification object. Required when the [`types`](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/#/ManagementService/v1/post/companies/{companyId}/webhooks/{webhookId}/test__reqParam_types) list contains **CUSTOM**.|
|» types|body|[string]|false|List of event codes for which to send test notifications. Only the webhook types below are supported. <br><br>Possible values if webhook `type`: **standard**:<br><br>* **AUTHORISATION**<br>* **CHARGEBACK_REVERSED**<br>* **ORDER_CLOSED**<br>* **ORDER_OPENED**<br>* **PAIDOUT_REVERSED**<br>* **PAYOUT_THIRDPARTY**<br>* **REFUNDED_REVERSED**<br>* **REFUND_WITH_DATA**<br>* **REPORT_AVAILABLE**<br>* **CUSTOM** - set your custom notification fields in the [`notification`](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/#/ManagementService/v1/post/companies/{companyId}/webhooks/{webhookId}/test__reqParam_notification) object.<br><br>Possible values if webhook `type`: **banktransfer-notification**:<br><br>* **PENDING**<br><br>Possible values if webhook `type`: **report-notification**:<br><br>* **REPORT_AVAILABLE**<br><br>Possible values if webhook `type`: **ideal-notification**:<br><br>* **AUTHORISATION**<br><br>Possible values if webhook `type`: **pending-notification**:<br><br>* **PENDING**<br>|

## List all webhooks

<a id="opIdget-merchants-merchantId-webhooks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/webhooks \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /merchants/{merchantId}/webhooks`

Lists all webhook configurations for the merchant account.

> This call does not return webhook configurations for the company account to which the specified merchant account belongs. You can see these in your Customer Area under **Developers** > **Webhooks**.

To make this request, your API credential must have one of the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Webhooks read
* Management API—Webhooks read and write

<h3 id="list-all-webhooks-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|
|pageNumber|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of the page to fetch.|
|pageSize|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of items to have on a page, maximum 100. The default is 10 items on a page.|

## Set up a webhook

<a id="opIdpost-merchants-merchantId-webhooks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/webhooks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "standard",
    "url": "YOUR_WEBHOOK_URL",
    "username": "YOUR_USER",
    "password": "YOUR_PASSWORD",
    "active": true,
    "communicationFormat": "json",
    "acceptsExpiredCertificate": false,
    "acceptsSelfSignedCertificate": true,
    "acceptsUntrustedRootCertificate": true,
    "populateSoapActionHeader": false
  }'
```

`POST /merchants/{merchantId}/webhooks`

Subscribe to receive webhook notifications about events related to your merchant account. You can add basic authentication to make sure the data is secure.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Webhooks read and write

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "standard",
  "url": "YOUR_WEBHOOK_URL",
  "username": "YOUR_USER",
  "password": "YOUR_PASSWORD",
  "active": true,
  "communicationFormat": "json",
  "acceptsExpiredCertificate": false,
  "acceptsSelfSignedCertificate": true,
  "acceptsUntrustedRootCertificate": true,
  "populateSoapActionHeader": false
}
```

<h3 id="set-up-a-webhook-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|
|body|body|[CreateMerchantWebhookRequest](#schemacreatemerchantwebhookrequest)|false|none|
|» acceptsExpiredCertificate|body|boolean|false|Indicates if expired SSL certificates are accepted. Default value: **false**.|
|» acceptsSelfSignedCertificate|body|boolean|false|Indicates if self-signed SSL certificates are accepted. Default value: **false**.|
|» acceptsUntrustedRootCertificate|body|boolean|false|Indicates if untrusted SSL certificates are accepted. Default value: **false**.|
|» active|body|boolean|true|Indicates if the webhook configuration is active. The field must be **true** for us to send webhooks about events related an account.|
|» additionalSettings|body|[AdditionalSettings](#schemaadditionalsettings)|false|Additional shopper and transaction information to be included in your [standard webhooks](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/webhooks/webhook-types/#event-codes). Find out more about the available [additional settings](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/webhooks/additional-settings).|
|» communicationFormat|body|string|true|Format or protocol for receiving webhooks. Possible values:<br>* **soap**<br>* **http**<br>* **json** |
|» description|body|string|false|Your description for this webhook configuration.|
|» encryptionProtocol|body|string|false|SSL version to access the public webhook URL specified in the `url` field. Possible values:<br>* **TLSv1.3**<br>* **TLSv1.2**<br>* **HTTP** - Only allowed on Test environment.<br><br>If not specified, the webhook will use `sslVersion`: **TLSv1.2**.|
|» networkType|body|string|false|Network type for Terminal API notification webhooks. Possible values:<br>* **public**<br>* **local**<br><br>Default Value: **public**.|
|» password|body|string|false|Password to access the webhook URL.|
|» populateSoapActionHeader|body|boolean|false|Indicates if the SOAP action header needs to be populated. Default value: **false**.<br><br>Only applies if `communicationFormat`: **soap**.|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of webhook that is being created. Possible values are:<br><br>- **standard**<br>- **account-settings-notification**<br>- **banktransfer-notification**<br>- **boletobancario-notification**<br>- **directdebit-notification**<br>- **ach-notification-of-change-notification**<br>- **direct-debit-notice-of-change-notification**<br>- **pending-notification**<br>- **ideal-notification**<br>- **ideal-pending-notification**<br>- **report-notification**<br>- **rreq-notification**<br>- **terminal-settings**<br>- **terminal-boarding**<br><br>Find out more about [standard webhooks](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/webhooks/webhook-types/#event-codes) and [other types of webhooks](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/webhooks/webhook-types/#other-webhooks).|
|» url|body|string|true|Public URL where webhooks will be sent, for example **https://www.domain.com/webhook-endpoint**.|
|» username|body|string|false|Username to access the webhook URL.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» communicationFormat|http|
|» communicationFormat|json|
|» communicationFormat|soap|
|» encryptionProtocol|HTTP|
|» encryptionProtocol|TLSv1.2|
|» encryptionProtocol|TLSv1.3|
|» networkType|local|
|» networkType|public|

## Update a webhook

<a id="opIdpatch-merchants-merchantId-webhooks-webhookId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/webhooks/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "active": true
  }'
```

`PATCH /merchants/{merchantId}/webhooks/{webhookId}`

Make changes to the configuration of the webhook identified in the path. The request contains the new values you want to have in the webhook configuration. The response contains the full configuration for the webhook, which includes the new values from the request.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Webhooks read and write

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "active": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-webhook-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|
|webhookId|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the webhook configuration.|
|body|body|[UpdateMerchantWebhookRequest](#schemaupdatemerchantwebhookrequest)|false|none|
|» acceptsExpiredCertificate|body|boolean|false|Indicates if expired SSL certificates are accepted. Default value: **false**.|
|» acceptsSelfSignedCertificate|body|boolean|false|Indicates if self-signed SSL certificates are accepted. Default value: **false**.|
|» acceptsUntrustedRootCertificate|body|boolean|false|Indicates if untrusted SSL certificates are accepted. Default value: **false**.|
|» active|body|boolean|false|Indicates if the webhook configuration is active. The field must be **true** for us to send webhooks about events related an account.|
|» additionalSettings|body|[AdditionalSettings](#schemaadditionalsettings)|false|Additional shopper and transaction information to be included in your [standard webhooks](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/webhooks/webhook-types/#event-codes). Find out more about the available [additional settings](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/webhooks/additional-settings).|
|» communicationFormat|body|string|false|Format or protocol for receiving webhooks. Possible values:<br>* **soap**<br>* **http**<br>* **json** |
|» description|body|string|false|Your description for this webhook configuration.|
|» encryptionProtocol|body|string|false|SSL version to access the public webhook URL specified in the `url` field. Possible values:<br>* **TLSv1.3**<br>* **TLSv1.2**<br>* **HTTP** - Only allowed on Test environment.<br><br>If not specified, the webhook will use `sslVersion`: **TLSv1.2**.|
|» networkType|body|string|false|Network type for Terminal API notification webhooks. Possible values:<br>* **public**<br>* **local**<br><br>Default Value: **public**.|
|» password|body|string|false|Password to access the webhook URL.|
|» populateSoapActionHeader|body|boolean|false|Indicates if the SOAP action header needs to be populated. Default value: **false**.<br><br>Only applies if `communicationFormat`: **soap**.|
|» url|body|string|false|Public URL where webhooks will be sent, for example **https://www.domain.com/webhook-endpoint**.|
|» username|body|string|false|Username to access the webhook URL.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» communicationFormat|http|
|» communicationFormat|json|
|» communicationFormat|soap|
|» encryptionProtocol|HTTP|
|» encryptionProtocol|TLSv1.2|
|» encryptionProtocol|TLSv1.3|
|» networkType|local|
|» networkType|public|

## Generate an HMAC key

<a id="opIdpost-merchants-merchantId-webhooks-webhookId-generateHmac"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/webhooks/string/generateHmac \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /merchants/{merchantId}/webhooks/{webhookId}/generateHmac`

Returns an [HMAC key](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMAC) for the webhook identified in the path. This key allows you to check the integrity and the origin of the notifications you receive.By creating an HMAC key, you start receiving [HMAC-signed notifications](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/webhooks/verify-hmac-signatures#enable-hmac-signatures) from Adyen. Find out more about how to [verify HMAC signatures](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/webhooks/verify-hmac-signatures).

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Webhooks read and write

<h3 id="generate-an-hmac-key-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|
|webhookId|path|string|true|none|
