## Test a webhook

<a id="opIdpost-merchants-merchantId-webhooks-webhookId-test"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/webhooks/string/test \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "types": [
      "AUTHORISATION"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /merchants/{merchantId}/webhooks/{webhookId}/test`

Sends sample notifications to test if the webhook is set up correctly.

We send four test notifications for each event code you choose. They cover success and failure scenarios for the hard-coded currencies EUR and GBP, regardless of the currencies configured in the merchant accounts. For custom notifications, we only send the specified custom notification.

The response describes the result of the test. The `status` field tells you if the test was successful or not. You can use the other fields to troubleshoot unsuccessful tests.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Webhooks read and write

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "types": [
    "AUTHORISATION"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="test-a-webhook-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|
|webhookId|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the webhook configuration.|
|body|body|[TestWebhookRequest](#schematestwebhookrequest)|false|none|
|» notification|body|[CustomNotification](#schemacustomnotification)|false|Custom test notification object. Required when the [`types`](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/#/ManagementService/v1/post/companies/{companyId}/webhooks/{webhookId}/test__reqParam_types) list contains **CUSTOM**.|
|» types|body|[string]|false|List of event codes for which to send test notifications. Only the webhook types below are supported. <br><br>Possible values if webhook `type`: **standard**:<br><br>* **AUTHORISATION**<br>* **CHARGEBACK_REVERSED**<br>* **ORDER_CLOSED**<br>* **ORDER_OPENED**<br>* **PAIDOUT_REVERSED**<br>* **PAYOUT_THIRDPARTY**<br>* **REFUNDED_REVERSED**<br>* **REFUND_WITH_DATA**<br>* **REPORT_AVAILABLE**<br>* **CUSTOM** - set your custom notification fields in the [`notification`](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/#/ManagementService/v1/post/companies/{companyId}/webhooks/{webhookId}/test__reqParam_notification) object.<br><br>Possible values if webhook `type`: **banktransfer-notification**:<br><br>* **PENDING**<br><br>Possible values if webhook `type`: **report-notification**:<br><br>* **REPORT_AVAILABLE**<br><br>Possible values if webhook `type`: **ideal-notification**:<br><br>* **AUTHORISATION**<br><br>Possible values if webhook `type`: **pending-notification**:<br><br>* **PENDING**<br>|

> Example responses

## Request a payment method

<a id="opIdpost-merchants-merchantId-paymentMethodSettings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/paymentMethodSettings \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "visa",
    "currencies": [
      "USD"
    ],
    "countries": [
      "US"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /merchants/{merchantId}/paymentMethodSettings`

Sends a request to add a new payment method to the merchant account identified in the path.
Depending the payment method [`type`](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/Management/latest/post/merchants/_merchantId_/paymentMethodSettings#request-type), you may need to send an additional object required for the payment method.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Payment methods read and write


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "visa",
  "currencies": [
    "USD"
  ],
  "countries": [
    "US"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="request-a-payment-method-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|
|body|body|[PaymentMethodSetupInfo](#schemapaymentmethodsetupinfo)|false|none|
|» accel|body|[AccelInfo](#schemaaccelinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **accel**.|
|» affirm|body|[AffirmInfo](#schemaaffirminfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **affirm**.|
|» afterpayTouch|body|[AfterpayTouchInfo](#schemaafterpaytouchinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **afterpaytouch**.|

|» amex|body|[AmexInfo](#schemaamexinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **amex**.<br>For merchants operating in Australia, New Zealand & Canada, JCB and American Express are automatically requested together.|
|» ancv|body|[AncvInfo](#schemaancvinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **ancv**.|
|» applePay|body|[ApplePayInfo](#schemaapplepayinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **applepay**.|
|» bcmc|body|[BcmcInfo](#schemabcmcinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **bcmc** (Bancontact).|
|» businessLineId|body|string|false|The unique identifier of the business line. Required if you are a [platform model](https://docs.adyen.com/platforms).|
|» carnet|body|[CarnetInfo](#schemacarnetinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **carnet**.|
|» cartesBancaires|body|[CartesBancairesInfo](#schemacartesbancairesinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **cartebancaire**.|
|» clearpay|body|[ClearpayInfo](#schemaclearpayinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **clearpay**.|
|» countries|body|[string]|false|The list of countries where a payment method is available. By default, all countries supported by the payment method.|
|» cup|body|[GenericPmWithTdiInfo](#schemagenericpmwithtdiinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **cup** (China Union Pay).|
|» currencies|body|[string]|false|The list of currencies that a payment method supports. By default, all currencies supported by the payment method.|
|» customRoutingFlags|body|[string]|false|The list of custom routing flags to route payment to the intended acquirer.|
|» diners|body|[DinersInfo](#schemadinersinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **diners**.<br>For merchants operating in Japan, Diners payments are processed through the JCB network. |» ebt|body|[EbtInfo](#schemaebtinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **ebt**.|

|» givex|body|[GivexInfo](#schemagivexinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **givex**.|

## Get payment method details

<a id="opIdget-merchants-merchantId-paymentMethodSettings-paymentMethodId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/paymentMethodSettings/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /merchants/{merchantId}/paymentMethodSettings/{paymentMethodId}`

Returns details for the merchant account and the payment method identified in the path.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Payment methods read


<h3 id="get-payment-method-details-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|
|paymentMethodId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the payment method.|

## Update a payment method

<a id="opIdpatch-merchants-merchantId-paymentMethodSettings-paymentMethodId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/paymentMethodSettings/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "currencies": [
      "EUR"
    ],
    "countries": [
      "NL"
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /merchants/{merchantId}/paymentMethodSettings/{paymentMethodId}`

Updates payment method details for the merchant account and the payment method identified in the path.
Depending the payment method [`type`](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/Management/latest/patch/merchants/_merchantId_/paymentMethodSettings#request-type), you may need to send an additional object required for the payment method.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Payment methods read and write


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "currencies": [
    "EUR"
  ],
  "countries": [
    "NL"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-payment-method-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|
|paymentMethodId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the payment method.|
|body|body|[UpdatePaymentMethodInfo](#schemaupdatepaymentmethodinfo)|false|none|
|» accel|body|[AccelUpdateInfo](#schemaaccelupdateinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **accel**.|
|» affirm|body|[AffirmUpdateInfo](#schemaaffirmupdateinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **affirm**.|
|» bcmc|body|[BcmcUpdateInfo](#schemabcmcupdateinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **bcmc** (Bancontact).|
|» carnet|body|[GenericPmWithTdiUpdateInfo](#schemagenericpmwithtdiupdateinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **carnet**.|
|» cartesBancaires|body|[CartesBancairesUpdateInfo](#schemacartesbancairesupdateinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **cartebancaire**.|
|» cashapp|body|[CashAppUpdateInfo](#schemacashappupdateinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **cashapp**.|
|» countries|body|[string]|false|The list of countries where a payment method is available. By default, all countries supported by the payment method.|
|» cup|body|[GenericPmWithTdiUpdateInfo](#schemagenericpmwithtdiupdateinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **cup** (China Union Pay).|
|» currencies|body|[string]|false|The list of currencies that a payment method supports. By default, all currencies supported by the payment method.|
|» customRoutingFlags|body|[string]|false|Custom routing flags for acquirer routing.|
|» diners|body|[GenericPmWithTdiUpdateInfo](#schemagenericpmwithtdiupdateinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **diners**.<br>For merchants operating in Japan, Diners payments are processed through the JCB network. This means that you must include [JCB-specific fields](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/Management/latest/post/merchants/(merchantId)/paymentMethodSettings/(paymentMethodId)#request-jcb) in this object.|
|» discover|body|[GenericPmWithTdiUpdateInfo](#schemagenericpmwithtdiupdateinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **discover**.<br>For merchants operating in Japan, request [Diners](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/Management/latest/post/merchants/(merchantId)/paymentMethodSettings/(paymentMethodId)#request-diners) payment method instead. Discover is automatically requested, together with Diners.|
|» ebt|body|[EbtUpdateInfo](#schemaebtupdateinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **ebt**.|
|» eft_directdebit_CA|body|[GenericPmWithTdiUpdateInfo](#schemagenericpmwithtdiupdateinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **eft_directdebit_CA** (EFT PAD).|
|» eftpos_australia|body|[GenericPmWithTdiUpdateInfo](#schemagenericpmwithtdiupdateinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **eftpos_australia**.|
|» enabled|body|boolean|false|Indicates whether the payment method is enabled (**true**) or disabled (**false**).|
|» girocard|body|[GenericPmWithTdiUpdateInfo](#schemagenericpmwithtdiupdateinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **girocard**.|
|» ideal|body|[GenericPmWithTdiUpdateInfo](#schemagenericpmwithtdiupdateinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **ideal**.|
|» interac_card|body|[GenericPmWithTdiUpdateInfo](#schemagenericpmwithtdiupdateinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **interac_card**.|
|» jcb|body|[GenericPmWithTdiUpdateInfo](#schemagenericpmwithtdiupdateinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **jcb**.<br>For merchants operating in Japan, `midNumber`, `reuseMidNumber`, and `serviceLevel` fields are required.<br>For merchants operating outside of Japan, these fields are not required.|
|» maestro|body|[GenericPmWithTdiUpdateInfo](#schemagenericpmwithtdiupdateinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **maestro**.<br>In the US, `maestro` is not supported; use `maestro_usa` instead. |
|» maestro_usa|body|[GenericPmWithTdiUpdateInfo](#schemagenericpmwithtdiupdateinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **maestro_usa**.<br>Only for Maestro USA, otherwise use `maestro`.|
|» mc|body|[GenericPmWithTdiUpdateInfo](#schemagenericpmwithtdiupdateinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **mc**.|
|» nyce|body|[NyceUpdateInfo](#schemanyceupdateinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **nyce**.|
|» paybybank_plaid|body|[PayByBankPlaidUpdateInfo](#schemapaybybankplaidupdateinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **paybybank_plaid**.|
|» pulse|body|[PulseUpdateInfo](#schemapulseupdateinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **pulse**.|
|» sepadirectdebit|body|[SepaDirectDebitUpdateInfo](#schemasepadirectdebitupdateinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **sepadirectdebit**.|
|» star|body|[StarUpdateInfo](#schemastarupdateinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **star**.|
|» storeId|body|string|false|The store for this payment method|
|» storeIds|body|[string]|false|**Deprecated.** The list of stores for this payment method|
|» visa|body|[GenericPmWithTdiUpdateInfo](#schemagenericpmwithtdiupdateinfo)|false|Details to provide if `type` is **visa**.|

## Add an Apple Pay domain

<a id="opIdpost-merchants-merchantId-paymentMethodSettings-paymentMethodId-addApplePayDomains"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/paymentMethodSettings/string/addApplePayDomains \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "domains": [
      "https://example.com"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /merchants/{merchantId}/paymentMethodSettings/{paymentMethodId}/addApplePayDomains`

Adds the new domain to the list of Apple Pay domains that are registered with the merchant account and the payment method identified in the path. For more information, see [Apple Pay documentation](https://docs.adyen.com/payment-methods/apple-pay/web-drop-in/?tab=adyen-certificate-live_1#going-live).

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Payment methods read and write


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "domains": [
    "https://example.com"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="add-an-apple-pay-domain-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|
|paymentMethodId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the payment method.|
|body|body|[ApplePayInfo](#schemaapplepayinfo)|false|none|
|» domains|body|[string]|true|The list of merchant domains. Maximum: 99 domains per request.<br><br>For more information, see [Apple Pay documentation](https://docs.adyen.com/payment-methods/apple-pay/web-drop-in?tab=adyen-certificate-live_1#going-live).|

<h1 id="management-api-terminals---terminal-level">Terminals - terminal level</h1>

## Get a list of terminals

<a id="opIdget-terminals"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/terminals \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /terminals`

Returns the payment terminals that the API credential has access to and that match the query parameters. 
To make this request, your API credential must have the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API — Terminal actions read

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

<h3 id="get-a-list-of-terminals-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|searchQuery|query|string|false|Returns terminals with an ID that contains the specified string. If present, other query parameters are ignored.|
|otpQuery|query|string|false|Returns one or more terminals associated with the one-time passwords specified in the request. If this query parameter is used, other query parameters are ignored.|
|countries|query|string|false|Returns terminals located in the countries specified by their [two-letter country code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2).|
|merchantIds|query|string|false|Returns terminals that belong to the merchant accounts specified by their unique merchant account ID.|
|storeIds|query|string|false|Returns terminals that are assigned to the [stores](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/#/ManagementService/latest/get/stores) specified by their unique store ID.|
|brandModels|query|string|false|Returns terminals of the [models](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/#/ManagementService/latest/get/companies/{companyId}/terminalModels) specified in the format *brand.model*.|
|pageNumber|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of the page to fetch.|
|pageSize|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of items to have on a page, maximum 100. The default is 20 items on a page.|

## Reassign a terminal

<a id="opIdpost-terminals-terminalId-reassign"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/terminals/string/reassign \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "merchantId": "YOUR_MERCHANT_ID",
    "inventory": false
  }'
```

`POST /terminals/{terminalId}/reassign`

Reassigns a payment terminal to a company account, merchant account, merchant account inventory, or a store.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Assign Terminal

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "merchantId": "YOUR_MERCHANT_ID",
  "inventory": false
}
```

<h3 id="reassign-a-terminal-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|terminalId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the payment terminal.|
|body|body|[TerminalReassignmentRequest](#schematerminalreassignmentrequest)|false|none|
|» companyId|body|string|false|The unique identifier of the company account to which the terminal is reassigned.|
|» inventory|body|boolean|false|Must be specified when reassigning terminals to a merchant account:<br><br>- If set to **true**, reassigns terminals to the inventory of the merchant account and the terminals cannot process transactions.<br><br>- If set to **false**, reassigns terminals directly to the merchant account and the terminals can process transactions.|
|» merchantId|body|string|false|The unique identifier of the merchant account to which the terminal is reassigned. When reassigning terminals to a merchant account, you must specify the `inventory` field.|
|» storeId|body|string|false|The unique identifier of the store to which the terminal is reassigned.|

## Get a list of terminal actions

<a id="opIdget-companies-companyId-terminalActions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/string/terminalActions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

```

`GET /companies/{companyId}/terminalActions`

Returns the [terminal actions](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management/terminal-actions-api) that have been scheduled for the company identified in the path.The response doesn't include actions that are scheduled by Adyen.
To make this request, your API credential must have one of the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Terminal actions read
* Management API—Terminal actions read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

|pageNumber|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of the page to fetch.|
|pageSize|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of items to have on a page, maximum 100. The default is 20 items on a page.|
|status|query|string|false|Returns terminal actions with the specified status. <br>Allowed values: **pending**, **successful**, **failed**, **cancelled**, **tryLater**.|

<h1 id="management-api-terminal-actions---terminal-level">Terminal actions - terminal level</h1>

## Create a terminal action

<a id="opIdpost-terminals-scheduleActions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/terminals/scheduleActions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "terminalIds": [
      "S1E-000150183300032",
      "S1E-000150183300033",
      "S1F2-000150183300034"
    ],
    "storeId": "",
    "scheduledAt": "2021-12-12T20:21:22-0100",
    "actionDetails": {
      "type": "InstallAndroidApp",
      "appId": "ANDA422LZ223223K5F694GCCF732K8"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /terminals/scheduleActions`

Schedules a [terminal action](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management/terminal-actions-api) by specifying the action and the terminals that the action must be applied to. 

The following restrictions apply:
* You can schedule only one action at a time. For example, to install a new app version and remove an old app version, you have to make two API requests. 
* The maximum number of terminals in a request is **100**. For example, to apply an action to 250 terminals, you have to divide the terminals over three API requests. 
* If there is an error with one or more terminal IDs in the request, the action is scheduled for none of the terminals. You need to fix the error and try again. 

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Terminal actions read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "terminalIds": [
    "S1E-000150183300032",
    "S1E-000150183300033",
    "S1F2-000150183300034"
  ],
  "storeId": "",
  "scheduledAt": "2021-12-12T20:21:22-0100",
  "actionDetails": {
    "type": "InstallAndroidApp",
    "appId": "ANDA422LZ223223K5F694GCCF732K8"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-terminal-action-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ScheduleTerminalActionsRequest](#schemascheduleterminalactionsrequest)|false|none|
|» actionDetails|body|[ForceRebootDetails](#schemaforcerebootdetails) \| [InstallAndroidAppDetails](#schemainstallandroidappdetails) \| [InstallAndroidCertificateDetails](#schemainstallandroidcertificatedetails) \| [ReleaseUpdateDetails](#schemareleaseupdatedetails) \| [UninstallAndroidAppDetails](#schemauninstallandroidappdetails) \| [UninstallAndroidCertificateDetails](#schemauninstallandroidcertificatedetails)|false|Information about the action to take.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[ForceRebootDetails](#schemaforcerebootdetails)|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[InstallAndroidAppDetails](#schemainstallandroidappdetails)|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[InstallAndroidCertificateDetails](#schemainstallandroidcertificatedetails)|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[ReleaseUpdateDetails](#schemareleaseupdatedetails)|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[UninstallAndroidAppDetails](#schemauninstallandroidappdetails)|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[UninstallAndroidCertificateDetails](#schemauninstallandroidcertificatedetails)|false|none|
|» scheduledAt|body|string|false|The date and time when the action should happen. <br>Format: [RFC 3339](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3339), but without the **Z** before the time offset. For example, **2021-11-15T12:16:21+0100** <br>The action is sent with the first [maintenance call](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management/terminal-actions-api#when-actions-take-effect) after the specified date and time in the time zone of the terminal. <br>An empty value causes the action to be sent as soon as possible: at the next maintenance call.|
|» storeId|body|string|false|The unique ID of the [store](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/#/ManagementService/latest/get/stores). If present, all terminals in the `terminalIds` list must be assigned to this store.|
|» terminalIds|body|[string]|false|A list of unique IDs of the terminals to apply the action to. You can extract the IDs from the [GET `/terminals`](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/#/ManagementService/latest/get/terminals) response. Maximum length: 100 IDs.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "actionDetails": {
    "appId": "ANDA422LZ223223K5F694GCCF732K8",
    "type": "InstallAndroidApp"
  },
  "scheduledAt": "2021-12-12T20:21:22-0100",
  "storeId": "",
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "TRAC422T2223223K5GFMQHM6WQ4KB6",
      "terminalId": "S1E-000150183300032"
    },
    {
      "id": "TRAC4224X22338VQ5GD4CQJCQT5PC2",
      "terminalId": "S1E-000150183300033"
    },
    {
      "id": "TRAC4224Z223223K5GD89RLBWQ6CWT",
      "terminalId": "S1F2-000150183300034"
    }
  ],
```

## Get a list of billing entities

<a id="opIdget-companies-companyId-billingEntities"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/string/billingEntities \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /companies/{companyId}/billingEntities`

Returns the billing entities of the company identified in the path and all merchant accounts belonging to the company.
A billing entity is a legal entity where we charge orders to. An order for terminal products must contain the ID of a billing entity.

To make this request, your API credential must have one of the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Terminal ordering read
* Management API—Terminal ordering read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

<h3 id="get-a-list-of-billing-entities-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|companyId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the company account.|
|name|query|string|false|The name of the billing entity.|

## Get a list of shipping locations

<a id="opIdget-companies-companyId-shippingLocations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/string/shippingLocations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /companies/{companyId}/shippingLocations`

Returns the shipping locations for the company identified in the path and all merchant accounts belonging to the company.
A shipping location includes the address where orders can be delivered, and an ID which you need to specify when ordering terminal products.

To make this request, your API credential must have one of the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Terminal ordering read
* Management API—Terminal ordering read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

<h3 id="get-a-list-of-shipping-locations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|companyId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the company account.|
|name|query|string|false|The name of the shipping location.|
|offset|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of locations to skip.|
|limit|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of locations to return.|

## Create a shipping location

<a id="opIdpost-companies-companyId-shippingLocations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/string/shippingLocations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "YOUR_COMPANY Rokin depot",
    "address": {
      "companyName": "YOUR_COMPANY",
      "streetAddress": "Rokin 21",
      "postalCode": "1012 KS",
      "city": "Amsterdam",
      "stateOrProvince": "",
      "country": "NL"
    },
    "contact": {
      "firstName": "Paul",
      "lastName": "Green",
      "phoneNumber": "+31 020 1234567",
      "email": "Paul.Green@company.com"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /companies/{companyId}/shippingLocations`

Creates a shipping location for the company identified in the path. A shipping location defines an address where orders can be delivered.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Terminal ordering read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "YOUR_COMPANY Rokin depot",
  "address": {
    "companyName": "YOUR_COMPANY",
    "streetAddress": "Rokin 21",
    "postalCode": "1012 KS",
    "city": "Amsterdam",
    "stateOrProvince": "",
    "country": "NL"
  },
  "contact": {
    "firstName": "Paul",
    "lastName": "Green",
    "phoneNumber": "+31 020 1234567",
    "email": "Paul.Green@company.com"
  }
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|companyId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the company account.|
|body|body|[ShippingLocation](#schemashippinglocation)|false|none|
|» address|body|[Address](#schemaaddress)|false|The address details of the shipping location.|
|» contact|body|[Contact](#schemacontact)|false|The contact details for the shipping location.|
|» id|body|string|false|The unique identifier of the shipping location, for use as `shippingLocationId` when creating an order.|
|» name|body|string|false|The unique name of the shipping location.|

## Get a list of orders

<a id="opIdget-companies-companyId-terminalOrders"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/string/terminalOrders \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /companies/{companyId}/terminalOrders`

Returns a lists of terminal products orders for the company identified in the path.
To filter the list, use one or more of the query parameters.

To make this request, your API credential must have one of the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Terminal ordering read
* Management API—Terminal ordering read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

<h3 id="get-a-list-of-orders-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|companyId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the company account.|
|customerOrderReference|query|string|false|Your purchase order number.|
|status|query|string|false|The order status. Possible values (not case-sensitive): Placed, Confirmed, Cancelled, Shipped, Delivered.|
|offset|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of orders to skip.|
|limit|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of orders to return.|

## Create an order

<a id="opIdpost-companies-companyId-terminalOrders"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/string/terminalOrders \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "customerOrderReference": "YOUR_REFERENCE",
    "shippingLocationId": "S2-6A6C2E3432747D4F2F2C3455485E3836457D",
    "billingEntityId": "Company.YOUR_COMPANY",
    "items": [
      {
        "id": "TBOX-V400m-684-EU",
        "name": "V400m Package",
        "quantity": 1
      },
      {
        "id": "PART-175746-EU",
        "name": "Adyen Test Card",
        "quantity": 1
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /companies/{companyId}/terminalOrders`

Creates an order for payment terminal products for the company identified in the path.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Terminal ordering read and write
>Requests to the Management API test endpoint do not create actual orders for test terminals. To order test terminals, you need to [submit a sales order](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/managing-terminals/order-terminals/#sales-order-steps) in your Customer Area.

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "customerOrderReference": "YOUR_REFERENCE",
  "shippingLocationId": "S2-6A6C2E3432747D4F2F2C3455485E3836457D",
  "billingEntityId": "Company.YOUR_COMPANY",
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "TBOX-V400m-684-EU",
      "name": "V400m Package",
      "quantity": 1
    },
    {
      "id": "PART-175746-EU",
      "name": "Adyen Test Card",
      "quantity": 1
    }
  ]
}
```

## Update an order

<a id="opIdpatch-companies-companyId-terminalOrders-orderId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/string/terminalOrders/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "items": [
      {
        "id": "TBOX-V400m-684-EU",
        "name": "V400m Package",
        "quantity": 1
      },
      {
        "id": "PART-175746-EU",
        "name": "Adyen Test Card",
        "quantity": 1
      },
      {
        "id": "PART-620222-EU",
        "name": "Receipt Roll",
        "quantity": 5
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /companies/{companyId}/terminalOrders/{orderId}`

Updates the terminal products order identified in the path.
Updating is only possible while the order has the status **Placed**.

The request body only needs to contain what you want to change. 
However, to update the products in the `items` array, you must provide the entire array. For example, if the array has three items:
 To remove one item, the array must include the remaining two items. Or to add one item, the array must include all four items.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Terminal ordering read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "TBOX-V400m-684-EU",
      "name": "V400m Package",
      "quantity": 1
    },
    {
      "id": "PART-175746-EU",
      "name": "Adyen Test Card",
      "quantity": 1
    },
    {
      "id": "PART-620222-EU",
      "name": "Receipt Roll",
      "quantity": 5
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-order-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|companyId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the company account.|
|orderId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the order.|
|body|body|[TerminalOrderRequest](#schematerminalorderrequest)|false|none|
|» billingEntityId|body|string|false|The identification of the billing entity to use for the order. <br><br> > When ordering products in Brazil, you do not need to include the `billingEntityId` in the request.|
|» customerOrderReference|body|string|false|The merchant-defined purchase order reference.|
|» items|body|[[OrderItem](#schemaorderitem)]|false|The products included in the order.|
|» orderType|body|string|false|Type of order|
|» shippingLocationId|body|string|false|The identification of the shipping location to use for the order.|
|» taxId|body|string|false|The tax number of the billing entity.|

## Cancel an order

<a id="opIdpost-companies-companyId-terminalOrders-orderId-cancel"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/string/terminalOrders/string/cancel \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /companies/{companyId}/terminalOrders/{orderId}/cancel`

Cancels the terminal products order identified in the path.
Cancelling is only possible while the order has the status **Placed**.
To cancel an order, make a POST call without a request body. The response returns the full order details, but with the status changed to **Cancelled**.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Terminal ordering read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

<h3 id="cancel-an-order-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|companyId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the company account.|
|orderId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the order.|

## Get a list of terminal products

<a id="opIdget-companies-companyId-terminalProducts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/string/terminalProducts?country=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /companies/{companyId}/terminalProducts`

Returns a country-specific list of payment terminal packages and parts that the company identified in the path has access to.
 
To make this request, your API credential must have one of the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Terminal ordering read
* Management API—Terminal ordering read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

<h3 id="get-a-list-of-terminal-products-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|companyId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the company account.|
|country|query|string|true|The country to return products for, in [ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2) format. For example, **US**|
|terminalModelId|query|string|false|The terminal model to return products for. Use the ID returned in the [GET `/terminalModels`](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/#/ManagementService/latest/get/companies/{companyId}/terminalModels) response. For example, **Verifone.M400**|
|offset|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of products to skip.|
|limit|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of products to return.|

## Get a list of billing entities

<a id="opIdget-merchants-merchantId-billingEntities"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/billingEntities \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /merchants/{merchantId}/billingEntities`

Returns the billing entities of the merchant account identified in the path.
A billing entity is a legal entity where we charge orders to. An order for terminal products must contain the ID of a billing entity.

To make this request, your API credential must have one of the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Terminal ordering read

|name|query|string|false|The name of the billing entity.|

## Get a list of shipping locations

<a id="opIdget-merchants-merchantId-shippingLocations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /merchants/{merchantId}/shippingLocations`

Returns the shipping locations for the merchant account identified in the path.
A shipping location includes the address where orders can be delivered, and an ID which you need to specify when ordering terminal products.

To make this request, your API credential must have one of the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Terminal ordering read

## Create a shipping location

<a id="opIdpost-merchants-merchantId-shippingLocations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/shippingLocations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

      "lastName": "Perengano",

    }
  }'
```

`POST /merchants/{merchantId}/shippingLocations`

Creates a shipping location for the merchant account identified in the path. A shipping location defines an address where orders can be shipped to. 

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Terminal ordering read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

`GET /merchants/{merchantId}/terminalModels`

## Get a list of orders

<a id="opIdget-merchants-merchantId-terminalOrders"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/terminalOrders \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /merchants/{merchantId}/terminalOrders`

Returns a list of terminal products orders for the merchant account identified in the path.

To make this request, your API credential must have one of the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Terminal ordering read
* Management API—Terminal ordering read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

<h3 id="get-a-list-of-orders-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|none|
|customerOrderReference|query|string|false|Your purchase order number.|
|status|query|string|false|The order status. Possible values (not case-sensitive): Placed, Confirmed, Cancelled, Shipped, Delivered.|
|offset|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of orders to skip.|
|limit|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of orders to return.|

## Create an order

<a id="opIdpost-merchants-merchantId-terminalOrders"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/terminalOrders \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "customerOrderReference": "YOUR_REFERENCE",
    "shippingLocationId": "S2-6A6C2E3432747D4F2F2C3455485E3836457D",
    "billingEntityId": "MerchantAccount.YOUR_MERCHANT_ACCOUNT",
    "items": [
      {
        "id": "PART-287001-EU",
        "name": "Bluetooth Charging Base - V400m",
        "quantity": 2
      },
      {
        "id": "PART-620222-EU",
        "name": "Receipt Roll",
        "quantity": 20
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /merchants/{merchantId}/terminalOrders`

Creates an order for payment terminal products for the merchant account identified in the path.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Terminal ordering read and write
>Requests to the Management API test endpoint do not create actual orders for test terminals. To order test terminals, you need to [submit a sales order](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/managing-terminals/order-terminals/#sales-order-steps) in your Customer Area.

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "customerOrderReference": "YOUR_REFERENCE",
  "shippingLocationId": "S2-6A6C2E3432747D4F2F2C3455485E3836457D",
  "billingEntityId": "MerchantAccount.YOUR_MERCHANT_ACCOUNT",
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "PART-287001-EU",
      "name": "Bluetooth Charging Base - V400m",
      "quantity": 2
    },
    {
      "id": "PART-620222-EU",
      "name": "Receipt Roll",
      "quantity": 20
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-order-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

## Update an order

<a id="opIdpatch-merchants-merchantId-terminalOrders-orderId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/terminalOrders/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "items": [
      {
        "id": "TBOX-V400m-684-EU",
        "name": "V400m Package",
        "quantity": 1
      },
      {
        "id": "PART-287001-EU",
        "name": "Bluetooth Charging Base - V400m",
        "quantity": 2
      },
      {
        "id": "PART-620222-EU",
        "name": "Receipt Roll",
        "quantity": 20
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /merchants/{merchantId}/terminalOrders/{orderId}`

Updates the terminal products order identified in the path.
Updating is only possible while the order has the status **Placed**.

The request body only needs to contain what you want to change. 
However, to update the products in the `items` array, you must provide the entire array. For example, if the array has three items:
 To remove one item, the array must include the remaining two items. Or to add one item, the array must include all four items.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Terminal ordering read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "TBOX-V400m-684-EU",
      "name": "V400m Package",
      "quantity": 1
    },
    {
      "id": "PART-287001-EU",
      "name": "Bluetooth Charging Base - V400m",
      "quantity": 2
    },
    {
      "id": "PART-620222-EU",
      "name": "Receipt Roll",
      "quantity": 20
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-order-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|
|orderId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the order.|
|body|body|[TerminalOrderRequest](#schematerminalorderrequest)|false|none|
|» billingEntityId|body|string|false|The identification of the billing entity to use for the order. <br><br> > When ordering products in Brazil, you do not need to include the `billingEntityId` in the request.|
|» customerOrderReference|body|string|false|The merchant-defined purchase order reference.|
|» items|body|[[OrderItem](#schemaorderitem)]|false|The products included in the order.|
|» orderType|body|string|false|Type of order|
|» shippingLocationId|body|string|false|The identification of the shipping location to use for the order.|
|» taxId|body|string|false|The tax number of the billing entity.|

## Cancel an order

<a id="opIdpost-merchants-merchantId-terminalOrders-orderId-cancel"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/terminalOrders/string/cancel \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /merchants/{merchantId}/terminalOrders/{orderId}/cancel`

Cancels the terminal products order identified in the path.
Cancelling is only possible while the order has the status **Placed**.
To cancel an order, make a POST call without a request body. The response returns the full order details, but with the status changed to **Cancelled**.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Terminal ordering read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

<h3 id="cancel-an-order-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|
|orderId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the order.|

## Get a list of terminal products

<a id="opIdget-merchants-merchantId-terminalProducts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/terminalProducts?country=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /merchants/{merchantId}/terminalProducts`

Returns a country-specific list of payment terminal packages and parts that the merchant account identified in the path has access to.

To make this request, your API credential must have one of the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Terminal ordering read
* Management API—Terminal ordering read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

## Get the terminal logo

<a id="opIdget-companies-companyId-terminalLogos"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/string/terminalLogos?model=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /companies/{companyId}/terminalLogos`

Returns the logo that is configured for a specific payment terminal model at the company identified in the path. 

The logo is returned as a Base64-encoded string. You need to Base64-decode the string to get the actual image file. 
This logo applies to all terminals of the specified model under the company, unless a different logo is configured at a lower level (merchant account, store, or individual terminal).

To make this request, your API credential must have one of the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Terminal settings read
* Management API—Terminal settings read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

<h3 id="get-the-terminal-logo-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|companyId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the company account.|
|model|query|string|true|The terminal model. Possible values: E355, VX675WIFIBT, VX680, VX690, VX700, VX820, M400, MX925, P400Plus, UX300, UX410, V200cPlus, V240mPlus, V400cPlus, V400m, e280, e285, e285p, S1E, S1EL, S1F2, S1L, S1U, S7T.|

## Update the terminal logo

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/string/terminalLogos?model=string' \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "data": ""
  }'
```

`PATCH /companies/{companyId}/terminalLogos`

Updates the logo that is configured for a specific payment terminal model at the company identified in the path. You can update the logo for only one terminal model at a time.
This logo applies to all terminals of the specified model under the company, unless a different logo is configured at a lower level (merchant account, store, or individual terminal). 
* To change the logo, specify the image file as a Base64-encoded string.
* To restore the logo inherited from the Adyen PSP level, specify an empty logo value.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Terminal settings read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": ""
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|companyId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the company account.|
|model|query|string|true|The terminal model. Possible values: E355, VX675WIFIBT, VX680, VX690, VX700, VX820, M400, MX925, P400Plus, UX300, UX410, V200cPlus, V240mPlus, V400cPlus, V400m, e280, e285, e285p, S1E, S1EL, S1F2, S1L, S1U, S7T.|
|body|body|[Logo](#schemalogo)|false|none|
|» data|body|string|false|The image file, converted to a Base64-encoded string, of the logo to be shown on the terminal.|

## Update terminal settings

<a id="opIdpatch-companies-companyId-terminalSettings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/string/terminalSettings \

  -d '{
    "wifiProfiles": {
      "profiles": [

          },

          "eapIntermediateCert": {
            "data": "PD3tUS1CRDdJTiGDR...EFoLS0tLQg=",
            "name": "eap-peap-client.pem"
          },
          "eapPwd": "EAP_PEAP_PASSWORD",
          "hiddenSsid": false,
          "name": "Profile-eap-peap-1",
```

`PATCH /companies/{companyId}/terminalSettings`

Updates payment terminal settings for the company identified in the path. These settings apply to all terminals under the company, unless different values are configured at a lower level (merchant account, store, or individual terminal).

* To change a parameter value, include the full object that contains the parameter, even if you don't want to change all parameters in the object.
* To restore a parameter value inherited from the Adyen PSP level, include the full object that contains the parameter, and specify an empty value for the parameter or omit the parameter.
* Objects that are not included in the request are not updated.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Terminal settings read and write

For [sensitive terminal settings](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management/configure-terminals-api#sensitive-terminal-settings), your API credential must have the following role:
* Management API—Terminal settings Advanced read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

<h3 id="update-terminal-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|companyId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the company account.|
|body|body|[TerminalSettings](#schematerminalsettings)|false|none|
|» cardholderReceipt|body|[CardholderReceipt](#schemacardholderreceipt)|false|Settings to define the header of the shopper receipt.|
|» connectivity|body|[Connectivity](#schemaconnectivity)|false|Settings for terminal connectivity features.|
|» dcc|body|[Dcc](#schemadcc)|false|Settings for Dynamic Currency Conversion (DCC).|

|» homeScreen|body|[HomeScreenSettings](#schemahomescreensettings)|false|Settings for the home screen.|

|» localization|body|[Localization](#schemalocalization)|false|Settings for localization.|

|» nexo|body|[Nexo](#schemanexo)|false|Settings for a Terminal API integration.|
|» offlineProcessing|body|[OfflineProcessing](#schemaofflineprocessing)|false|Settings for EMV [offline payment](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/offline-payments) features.|
|» opi|body|[Opi](#schemaopi)|false|Settings for an Oracle Payment Interface (OPI) integration.|
|» passcodes|body|[Passcodes](#schemapasscodes)|false|Settings for [passcodes](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/managing-terminals/menu-access?tab=manage_passcodes_with_an_api_call_2#manage-passcodes) features.|
|» payAtTable|body|[PayAtTable](#schemapayattable)|false|Settings for [Pay-at-table](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/pay-at-x) features.|
|» payment|body|[Payment](#schemapayment)|false|Settings for payment features.|
|» receiptOptions|body|[ReceiptOptions](#schemareceiptoptions)|false|Generic receipt settings.|
|» receiptPrinting|body|[ReceiptPrinting](#schemareceiptprinting)|false|Transaction outcomes that you want the terminal to print a merchant receipt or a shopper receipt for.|
|» refunds|body|[Refunds](#schemarefunds)|false|Settings for refunds.|

|» standalone|body|[Standalone](#schemastandalone)|false|Settings for [standalone](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/standalone/standalone-build/set-up-standalone#set-up-standalone-using-an-api-call) features.|
|» storeAndForward|body|[StoreAndForward](#schemastoreandforward)|false|Settings for store-and-forward offline payments. The `maxAmount`, `maxPayments`, and `supportedCardTypes` parameters must be configured, either in the request or inherited from a higher level in your account structure.|
|» surcharge|body|[Surcharge](#schemasurcharge)|false|Settings for payment [surcharge](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/surcharge) features.|
|» tapToPay|body|[TapToPay](#schemataptopay)|false|Settings for Tap to Pay.|
|» terminalInstructions|body|[TerminalInstructions](#schematerminalinstructions)|false|Settings to define the behaviour of the payment terminal.|
|» timeouts|body|[Timeouts](#schematimeouts)|false|Settings for device [time-outs](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/pos-timeouts#device-time-out).|
|» wifiProfiles|body|[WifiProfiles](#schemawifiprofiles)|false|Remote Wi-Fi profiles for WPA and WPA2 PSK and EAP Wi-Fi networks.|

<h1 id="management-api-terminal-settings---merchant-level">Terminal settings - merchant level</h1>

## Get the terminal logo

<a id="opIdget-merchants-merchantId-terminalLogos"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/terminalLogos?model=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /merchants/{merchantId}/terminalLogos`

Returns the logo that is configured for a specific payment terminal model at the merchant account identified in the path. 
The logo is returned as a Base64-encoded string. You need to Base64-decode the string to get the actual image file. 
This logo applies to all terminals of the specified model under the merchant account, unless a different logo is configured at a lower level (store or individual terminal).

To make this request, your API credential must have one of the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Terminal settings read
* Management API—Terminal settings read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

<h3 id="get-the-terminal-logo-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|
|model|query|string|true|The terminal model. Possible values: E355, VX675WIFIBT, VX680, VX690, VX700, VX820, M400, MX925, P400Plus, UX300, UX410, V200cPlus, V240mPlus, V400cPlus, V400m, e280, e285, e285p, S1E, S1EL, S1F2, S1L, S1U, S7T.|

## Update the terminal logo

<a id="opIdpatch-merchants-merchantId-terminalLogos"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/terminalLogos?model=string' \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "data": ""
  }'
```

`PATCH /merchants/{merchantId}/terminalLogos`

Updates the logo for a specific payment terminal model at the merchant account identified in the path. You can update the logo for only one terminal model at a time. 
This logo applies to all terminals of the specified model under the merchant account, unless a different logo is configured at a lower level (store or individual terminal).

* To change the logo, specify the image file as a Base64-encoded string.
* To restore the logo inherited from the company account, specify an empty logo value.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Terminal settings read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": ""
}
```

<h3 id="update-the-terminal-logo-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|
|model|query|string|true|The terminal model. Allowed values: E355, VX675WIFIBT, VX680, VX690, VX700, VX820, M400, MX925, P400Plus, UX300, UX410, V200cPlus, V240mPlus, V400cPlus, V400m, e280, e285, e285p, S1E, S1EL, S1F2, S1L, S1U, S7T.|
|body|body|[Logo](#schemalogo)|false|none|
|» data|body|string|false|The image file, converted to a Base64-encoded string, of the logo to be shown on the terminal.|

## Get terminal settings

<a id="opIdget-merchants-merchantId-terminalSettings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/terminalSettings \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /merchants/{merchantId}/terminalSettings`

Returns the payment terminal settings that are configured for the merchant account identified in the path. These settings apply to all terminals under the merchant account unless different values are configured at a lower level (store or individual terminal).

To make this request, your API credential must have one of the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Terminal settings read
* Management API—Terminal settings read and write

For [sensitive terminal settings](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management/configure-terminals-api#sensitive-terminal-settings), your API credential must have the following role:
* Management API—Terminal settings Advanced read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

## Update terminal settings

<a id="opIdpatch-merchants-merchantId-terminalSettings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/terminalSettings \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "wifiProfiles": {
      "profiles": [
        {

          "autoWifi": false,

          "channel": 0,

        },

```

`PATCH /merchants/{merchantId}/terminalSettings`

Updates payment terminal settings for the merchant account identified in the path.
These settings apply to all terminals under the merchant account, unless different values are configured at a lower level (store or individual terminal).

* To change a parameter value, include the full object that contains the parameter, even if you don't want to change all parameters in the object.
* To restore a parameter value inherited from a higher level, include the full object that contains the parameter, and specify an empty value for the parameter or omit the parameter.
* Objects that are not included in the request are not updated.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Terminal settings read and write



For [sensitive terminal settings](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management/configure-terminals-api#sensitive-terminal-settings), your API credential must have the following role:
* Management API—Terminal settings Advanced read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

> Body parameter

<h1 id="management-api-terminal-settings---store-level">Terminal settings - store level</h1>

## Get the terminal logo

<a id="opIdget-merchants-merchantId-stores-reference-terminalLogos"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/stores/string/terminalLogos?model=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /merchants/{merchantId}/stores/{reference}/terminalLogos`

Returns the logo that is configured for a specific payment terminal model at the store identified in the path. 
The logo is returned as a Base64-encoded string. You need to Base64-decode the string to get the actual image file. 
This logo applies to all terminals of the specified model under the store, unless a different logo is configured for an individual terminal.

To make this request, your API credential must have one of the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Terminal settings read
* Management API—Terminal settings read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

<h3 id="get-the-terminal-logo-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|
|reference|path|string|true|The reference that identifies the store.|
|model|query|string|true|The terminal model. Possible values: E355, VX675WIFIBT, VX680, VX690, VX700, VX820, M400, MX925, P400Plus, UX300, UX410, V200cPlus, V240mPlus, V400cPlus, V400m, e280, e285, e285p, S1E, S1EL, S1F2, S1L, S1U, S7T.|

## Update the terminal logo

```bash
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "data": ""
  }'
```

`PATCH /merchants/{merchantId}/stores/{reference}/terminalLogos`

Updates the logo that is configured for a specific payment terminal model at the store identified in the path. You can update the logo for only one terminal model at a time.
This logo applies to all terminals of the specified model under the store, unless a different logo is configured for an individual terminal. 

* To change the logo, specify the image file as a Base64-encoded string.
* To restore the logo inherited from a higher level (merchant or company account), specify an empty logo value.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Terminal settings read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": ""
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|
|reference|path|string|true|The reference that identifies the store.|
|model|query|string|true|The terminal model. Possible values: E355, VX675WIFIBT, VX680, VX690, VX700, VX820, M400, MX925, P400Plus, UX300, UX410, V200cPlus, V240mPlus, V400cPlus, V400m, e280, e285, e285p, S1E, S1EL, S1F2, S1L, S1U, S7T|
|body|body|[Logo](#schemalogo)|false|none|
|» data|body|string|false|The image file, converted to a Base64-encoded string, of the logo to be shown on the terminal.|

## Get terminal settings

<a id="opIdget-merchants-merchantId-stores-reference-terminalSettings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/stores/string/terminalSettings \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /merchants/{merchantId}/stores/{reference}/terminalSettings`

Returns the payment terminal settings that are configured for the store identified in the path. These settings apply to all terminals under the store unless different values are configured for an individual terminal.

To make this request, your API credential must have one of the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Terminal settings read
* Management API—Terminal settings read and write

For [sensitive terminal settings](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management/configure-terminals-api#sensitive-terminal-settings), your API credential must have the following role:
* Management API—Terminal settings Advanced read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

<h3 id="get-terminal-settings-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|
|reference|path|string|true|The reference that identifies the store.|

## Update terminal settings

<a id="opIdpatch-merchants-merchantId-stores-reference-terminalSettings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/stores/string/terminalSettings \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "wifiProfiles": {
      "profiles": [
        {
          "authType": "wpa-eap",
          "autoWifi": false,
          "bssType": "infra",
          "channel": 0,
          "defaultProfile": true,
          "eap": "peap",
          "eapCaCert": {
            "data": "MD1rKS05M2JqRVFNQ...RTtLH1tLWo=",
            "name": "eap-peap-ca.pem"
          },
          "eapIdentity": "admin",
          "eapIntermediateCert": {
            "data": "PD3tUS1CRDdJTiGDR...EFoLS0tLQg=",
            "name": "eap-peap-client.pem"
          },
          "eapPwd": "EAP_PEAP_PASSWORD",
          "name": "Profile-eap-peap-1",
          "ssid": "your-network",
          "wsec": "ccmp"
        },
        {
          "authType": "wpa-psk",
          "autoWifi": false,
          "bssType": "infra",
          "channel": 0,
          "defaultProfile": false,
          "name": "Profile-guest-wifi",
          "psk": "WIFI_PASSWORD",
          "ssid": "your-network",
          "wsec": "ccmp"
        }
      ],
      "settings": {
        "band": "2.4GHz",
        "roaming": true,
        "timeout": 5
      }
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /merchants/{merchantId}/stores/{reference}/terminalSettings`

Updates payment terminal settings for the store identified in the path. These settings apply to all terminals under the store, unless different values are configured for an individual terminal.

* To change a parameter value, include the full object that contains the parameter, even if you don't want to change all parameters in the object.
* To restore a parameter value inherited from a higher level, include the full object that contains the parameter, and specify an empty value for the parameter or omit the parameter.
* Objects that are not included in the request are not updated.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Terminal settings read and write

For [sensitive terminal settings](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management/configure-terminals-api#sensitive-terminal-settings), your API credential must have the following role:
* Management API—Terminal settings Advanced read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

<h3 id="update-terminal-settings-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|
|reference|path|string|true|The reference that identifies the store.|
|body|body|[TerminalSettings](#schematerminalsettings)|false|none|
|» cardholderReceipt|body|[CardholderReceipt](#schemacardholderreceipt)|false|Settings to define the header of the shopper receipt.|
|» connectivity|body|[Connectivity](#schemaconnectivity)|false|Settings for terminal connectivity features.|
|» dcc|body|[Dcc](#schemadcc)|false|Settings for Dynamic Currency Conversion (DCC).|
|» gratuities|body|[[Gratuity](#schemagratuity)]|false|Settings for tipping with or without predefined options to choose from. The maximum number of predefined options is four, or three plus the option to enter a custom tip.|
|» hardware|body|[Hardware](#schemahardware)|false|Settings for terminal hardware features.|
|» homeScreen|body|[HomeScreenSettings](#schemahomescreensettings)|false|Settings for the home screen.|
|» kioskMode|body|[KioskModeSettings](#schemakioskmodesettings)|false|Settings for kiosk mode.|
|» localization|body|[Localization](#schemalocalization)|false|Settings for localization.|
|» moto|body|[Moto](#schemamoto)|false|Settings for Mail Order/Telephone Order transactions.|
|» nexo|body|[Nexo](#schemanexo)|false|Settings for a Terminal API integration.|
|» offlineProcessing|body|[OfflineProcessing](#schemaofflineprocessing)|false|Settings for EMV [offline payment](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/offline-payments) features.|
|» opi|body|[Opi](#schemaopi)|false|Settings for an Oracle Payment Interface (OPI) integration.|
|» passcodes|body|[Passcodes](#schemapasscodes)|false|Settings for [passcodes](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/managing-terminals/menu-access?tab=manage_passcodes_with_an_api_call_2#manage-passcodes) features.|
|» payAtTable|body|[PayAtTable](#schemapayattable)|false|Settings for [Pay-at-table](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/pay-at-x) features.|
|» payment|body|[Payment](#schemapayment)|false|Settings for payment features.|
|» receiptOptions|body|[ReceiptOptions](#schemareceiptoptions)|false|Generic receipt settings.|
|» receiptPrinting|body|[ReceiptPrinting](#schemareceiptprinting)|false|Transaction outcomes that you want the terminal to print a merchant receipt or a shopper receipt for.|
|» refunds|body|[Refunds](#schemarefunds)|false|Settings for refunds.|
|» showCalculatedPercentageTippingAmount|body|boolean \| null|false|Show the tipping amount calculated from the percentage next to each tipping percentage option on the terminal screen, for example `10 % \| 10 EUR` for a 100 EUR payment.|
|» signature|body|[Signature](#schemasignature)|false|Settings to skip signature, sign on display, or sign on receipt.|
|» standalone|body|[Standalone](#schemastandalone)|false|Settings for [standalone](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/standalone/standalone-build/set-up-standalone#set-up-standalone-using-an-api-call) features.|
|» storeAndForward|body|[StoreAndForward](#schemastoreandforward)|false|Settings for store-and-forward offline payments. The `maxAmount`, `maxPayments`, and `supportedCardTypes` parameters must be configured, either in the request or inherited from a higher level in your account structure.|
|» surcharge|body|[Surcharge](#schemasurcharge)|false|Settings for payment [surcharge](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/surcharge) features.|
|» tapToPay|body|[TapToPay](#schemataptopay)|false|Settings for Tap to Pay.|
|» terminalInstructions|body|[TerminalInstructions](#schematerminalinstructions)|false|Settings to define the behaviour of the payment terminal.|
|» timeouts|body|[Timeouts](#schematimeouts)|false|Settings for device [time-outs](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/pos-timeouts#device-time-out).|
|» wifiProfiles|body|[WifiProfiles](#schemawifiprofiles)|false|Remote Wi-Fi profiles for WPA and WPA2 PSK and EAP Wi-Fi networks.|

## Get the terminal logo

<a id="opIdget-stores-storeId-terminalLogos"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/stores/string/terminalLogos?model=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /stores/{storeId}/terminalLogos`

Returns the logo that is configured for a specific payment terminal model at the store identified in the path. 
The logo is returned as a Base64-encoded string. You need to Base64-decode the string to get the actual image file. 
This logo applies to all terminals of that model under the store unless a different logo is configured for an individual terminal.

To make this request, your API credential must have one of the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Terminal settings read
* Management API—Terminal settings read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

<h3 id="get-the-terminal-logo-3-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|storeId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the store.|
|model|query|string|true|The terminal model. Possible values: E355, VX675WIFIBT, VX680, VX690, VX700, VX820, M400, MX925, P400Plus, UX300, UX410, V200cPlus, V240mPlus, V400cPlus, V400m, e280, e285, e285p, S1E, S1EL, S1F2, S1L, S1U, S7T.|

## Update the terminal logo

<a id="opIdpatch-stores-storeId-terminalLogos"></a>

```bash
curl 'https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/stores/string/terminalLogos?model=string' \
```
