```bash
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "data": ""
  }'
```

`PATCH /stores/{storeId}/terminalLogos`

Updates the logo that is configured for a specific payment terminal model at the store identified in the path. You can update the logo for only one terminal model at a time.
This logo applies to all terminals of the specified model under the store, unless a different logo is configured for an individual terminal. 

* To change the logo, specify the image file as a Base64-encoded string.
* To restore the logo inherited from a higher level (merchant or company account), specify an empty logo value.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Terminal settings read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": ""
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|storeId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the store.|
|model|query|string|true|The terminal model. Possible values: E355, VX675WIFIBT, VX680, VX690, VX700, VX820, M400, MX925, P400Plus, UX300, UX410, V200cPlus, V240mPlus, V400cPlus, V400m, e280, e285, e285p, S1E, S1EL, S1F2, S1L, S1U, S7T.|
|body|body|[Logo](#schemalogo)|false|none|
|» data|body|string|false|The image file, converted to a Base64-encoded string, of the logo to be shown on the terminal.|

`GET /stores/{storeId}/terminalSettings`

Returns the payment terminal settings that are configured for the store identified in the path. These settings apply to all terminals under the store unless different values are configured for an individual terminal.

To make this request, your API credential must have one of the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):

* Management API—Terminal settings read and write

For [sensitive terminal settings](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management/configure-terminals-api#sensitive-terminal-settings), your API credential must have the following role:

`PATCH /stores/{storeId}/terminalSettings`

Updates payment terminal settings for the store identified in the path. These settings apply to all terminals under the store, unless different values are configured for an individual terminal.

* To change a parameter value, include the full object that contains the parameter, even if you don't want to change all parameters in the object.
* To restore a parameter value inherited from a higher level, include the full object that contains the parameter, and specify an empty value for the parameter or omit the parameter.
* Objects that are not included in the request are not updated.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Terminal settings read and write

For [sensitive terminal settings](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management/configure-terminals-api#sensitive-terminal-settings), your API credential must have the following role:
* Management API—Terminal settings Advanced read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

> Body parameter

```json
        "hiddenSsid": false,

    }

}
```

<h3 id="update-terminal-settings-3-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|storeId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the store.|
|body|body|[TerminalSettings](#schematerminalsettings)|false|none|

|» standalone|body|[Standalone](#schemastandalone)|false|Settings for [standalone](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/standalone/standalone-build/set-up-standalone#set-up-standalone-using-an-api-call) features.|
|» storeAndForward|body|[StoreAndForward](#schemastoreandforward)|false|Settings for store-and-forward offline payments. The `maxAmount`, `maxPayments`, and `supportedCardTypes` parameters must be configured, either in the request or inherited from a higher level in your account structure.|

|» tapToPay|body|[TapToPay](#schemataptopay)|false|Settings for Tap to Pay.|
|» terminalInstructions|body|[TerminalInstructions](#schematerminalinstructions)|false|Settings to define the behaviour of the payment terminal.|
|» timeouts|body|[Timeouts](#schematimeouts)|false|Settings for device [time-outs](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/pos-timeouts#device-time-out).|
|» wifiProfiles|body|[WifiProfiles](#schemawifiprofiles)|false|Remote Wi-Fi profiles for WPA and WPA2 PSK and EAP Wi-Fi networks.|

<a id="opIdpatch-terminals-terminalId-terminalSettings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash

  -d '{
    "wifiProfiles": {
      "profiles": [
        {
          "authType": "wpa-eap",

            "name": "eap-peap-client.pem"
          },
          "eapPwd": "EAP_PEAP_PASSWORD",
          "hiddenSsid": false,
          "name": "Profile-eap-peap-1",
          "ssid": "your-network",

        {

          "autoWifi": false,
          "bssType": "infra",

      }

```

`PATCH /terminals/{terminalId}/terminalSettings`

Updates the settings that are configured for the payment terminal identified in the path.

* To change a parameter value, include the full object that contains the parameter, even if you don't want to change all parameters in the object.
* To restore a parameter value inherited from a higher level, include the full object that contains the parameter, and specify an empty value for the parameter or omit the parameter.
* Objects that are not included in the request are not updated.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Terminal settings read and write

For [sensitive terminal settings](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management/configure-terminals-api#sensitive-terminal-settings), your API credential must have the following role:
* Management API—Terminal settings Advanced read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "wifiProfiles": {
    "profiles": [
      {
        "authType": "wpa-eap",
        "autoWifi": false,
        "bssType": "infra",
        "channel": 0,
        "defaultProfile": true,
        "eap": "peap",
        "eapCaCert": {
          "data": "MD1rKS05M2JqRVFNQ...RTtLH1tLWo=",
          "name": "eap-peap-ca.pem"
        },
        "eapIdentity": "admin",
        "eapIntermediateCert": {
          "data": "PD3tUS1CRDdJTiGDR...EFoLS0tLQg=",
          "name": "eap-peap-client.pem"
        },
        "eapPwd": "EAP_PEAP_PASSWORD",
        "hiddenSsid": false,
        "name": "Profile-eap-peap-1",
        "ssid": "your-network",
        "wsec": "ccmp"
      },
      {
        "authType": "wpa-psk",
        "autoWifi": false,
        "bssType": "infra",
        "channel": 0,
        "defaultProfile": false,
        "hiddenSsid": false,
        "name": "Profile-guest-wifi",
        "psk": "WIFI_PASSWORD",
        "ssid": "your-network",
        "wsec": "ccmp"
      }
    ],
    "settings": {
      "band": "2.4GHz",
      "roaming": true,
      "timeout": 5
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-terminal-settings-4-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|terminalId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the payment terminal.|
|body|body|[TerminalSettings](#schematerminalsettings)|false|none|
|» cardholderReceipt|body|[CardholderReceipt](#schemacardholderreceipt)|false|Settings to define the header of the shopper receipt.|
|» connectivity|body|[Connectivity](#schemaconnectivity)|false|Settings for terminal connectivity features.|
|» dcc|body|[Dcc](#schemadcc)|false|Settings for Dynamic Currency Conversion (DCC).|
|» gratuities|body|[[Gratuity](#schemagratuity)]|false|Settings for tipping with or without predefined options to choose from. The maximum number of predefined options is four, or three plus the option to enter a custom tip.|
|» hardware|body|[Hardware](#schemahardware)|false|Settings for terminal hardware features.|
|» homeScreen|body|[HomeScreenSettings](#schemahomescreensettings)|false|Settings for the home screen.|
|» kioskMode|body|[KioskModeSettings](#schemakioskmodesettings)|false|Settings for kiosk mode.|
|» localization|body|[Localization](#schemalocalization)|false|Settings for localization.|
|» moto|body|[Moto](#schemamoto)|false|Settings for Mail Order/Telephone Order transactions.|
|» nexo|body|[Nexo](#schemanexo)|false|Settings for a Terminal API integration.|
|» offlineProcessing|body|[OfflineProcessing](#schemaofflineprocessing)|false|Settings for EMV [offline payment](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/offline-payments) features.|
|» opi|body|[Opi](#schemaopi)|false|Settings for an Oracle Payment Interface (OPI) integration.|
|» passcodes|body|[Passcodes](#schemapasscodes)|false|Settings for [passcodes](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/managing-terminals/menu-access?tab=manage_passcodes_with_an_api_call_2#manage-passcodes) features.|
|» payAtTable|body|[PayAtTable](#schemapayattable)|false|Settings for [Pay-at-table](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/pay-at-x) features.|
|» payment|body|[Payment](#schemapayment)|false|Settings for payment features.|
|» receiptOptions|body|[ReceiptOptions](#schemareceiptoptions)|false|Generic receipt settings.|
|» receiptPrinting|body|[ReceiptPrinting](#schemareceiptprinting)|false|Transaction outcomes that you want the terminal to print a merchant receipt or a shopper receipt for.|
|» refunds|body|[Refunds](#schemarefunds)|false|Settings for refunds.|
|» showCalculatedPercentageTippingAmount|body|boolean \| null|false|Show the tipping amount calculated from the percentage next to each tipping percentage option on the terminal screen, for example `10 % \| 10 EUR` for a 100 EUR payment.|
|» signature|body|[Signature](#schemasignature)|false|Settings to skip signature, sign on display, or sign on receipt.|
|» standalone|body|[Standalone](#schemastandalone)|false|Settings for [standalone](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/standalone/standalone-build/set-up-standalone#set-up-standalone-using-an-api-call) features.|
|» storeAndForward|body|[StoreAndForward](#schemastoreandforward)|false|Settings for store-and-forward offline payments. The `maxAmount`, `maxPayments`, and `supportedCardTypes` parameters must be configured, either in the request or inherited from a higher level in your account structure.|
|» surcharge|body|[Surcharge](#schemasurcharge)|false|Settings for payment [surcharge](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/surcharge) features.|
|» tapToPay|body|[TapToPay](#schemataptopay)|false|Settings for Tap to Pay.|
|» terminalInstructions|body|[TerminalInstructions](#schematerminalinstructions)|false|Settings to define the behaviour of the payment terminal.|
|» timeouts|body|[Timeouts](#schematimeouts)|false|Settings for device [time-outs](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/pos-timeouts#device-time-out).|
|» wifiProfiles|body|[WifiProfiles](#schemawifiprofiles)|false|Remote Wi-Fi profiles for WPA and WPA2 PSK and EAP Wi-Fi networks.|

<h1 id="management-api-android-files---company-level">Android files - company level</h1>

## Get a list of Android apps

<a id="opIdget-companies-companyId-androidApps"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/string/androidApps \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /companies/{companyId}/androidApps`

Returns a list of the Android apps that are available for the company identified in the path. 
These apps have been uploaded to Adyen and can be installed or uninstalled on Android payment terminals through [terminal actions](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management/terminal-actions-api).

To make this request, your API credential must have one of the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Android files read
* Management API—Android files read and write
* Management API—Terminal actions read
* Management API—Terminal actions read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

<h3 id="get-a-list-of-android-apps-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|companyId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the company account.|
|pageNumber|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of the page to fetch.|
|pageSize|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of items to have on a page, maximum 100. The default is 20 items on a page.|
|packageName|query|string|false|The package name that uniquely identifies the Android app.|
|versionCode|query|integer(int32)|false|The version number of the app.|

> Example responses

## Upload Android App

<a id="opIdpost-companies-companyId-androidApps"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/string/androidApps \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /companies/{companyId}/androidApps`

Uploads an Android APK file to Adyen.
The maximum APK file size is 200 MB.
To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Android files read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).
>By choosing to upload, install, or run any third-party applications on an Adyen payment terminal, you accept full responsibility and liability for any consequences of uploading, installing, or running any such applications.

## Get a list of Android certificates

<a id="opIdget-companies-companyId-androidCertificates"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/string/androidCertificates \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /companies/{companyId}/androidCertificates`

Returns a list of the Android certificates that are available for the company identified in the path.
Typically, these certificates enable running apps on Android payment terminals. The certificates in the list have been uploaded to Adyen and can be installed or uninstalled on Android terminals through [terminal actions](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management/terminal-actions-api).

To make this request, your API credential must have one of the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Android files read
* Management API—Android files read and write
* Management API—Terminal actions read
* Management API—Terminal actions read and write

In the live environment, requests to this endpoint are subject to [rate limits](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

<h3 id="get-a-list-of-android-certificates-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|companyId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the company account.|
|pageNumber|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of the page to fetch.|
|pageSize|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of items to have on a page, maximum 100. The default is 20 items on a page.|
|certificateName|query|string|false|The name of the certificate.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

## Create a split configuration profile

<a id="opIdpost-merchants-merchantId-splitConfigurations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/splitConfigurations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "Your description for the split configuration",
    "rules": [
      {
        "paymentMethod": "ANY",
        "shopperInteraction": "ANY",
        "fundingSource": "ANY",
        "currency": "ANY",
        "splitLogic": {
          "paymentFee": "deductFromLiableAccount",
          "chargeback": "deductFromLiableAccount",
          "tip": "addToOneBalanceAccount",
          "remainder": "addToOneBalanceAccount",
          "commission": {
            "fixedAmount": 10,
            "variablePercentage": 100
          },
          "additionalCommission": {
            "fixedAmount": 10,
            "variablePercentage": 50,
            "balanceAccountId": "BA3227C223222H5HQ2XX77VVH"
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /merchants/{merchantId}/splitConfigurations`

Creates a split configuration profile to [split payments automatically](https://docs.adyen.com/platforms/automatic-split-configuration/). After you [associate it with a store](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/Management/latest/patch/merchants/(merchantId)/stores/(storeId)#request-splitConfiguration) in your merchant account, it splits the funds of all transactions processed through that store between your liable balance account and [your user's balance account](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/Management/latest/patch/merchants/(merchantId)/stores/(storeId)#request-splitConfiguration-balanceAccountId).

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API - SplitConfiguration read and write

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "Your description for the split configuration",
  "rules": [
    {
      "paymentMethod": "ANY",
      "shopperInteraction": "ANY",
      "fundingSource": "ANY",
      "currency": "ANY",
      "splitLogic": {
        "paymentFee": "deductFromLiableAccount",
        "chargeback": "deductFromLiableAccount",
        "tip": "addToOneBalanceAccount",
        "remainder": "addToOneBalanceAccount",
        "commission": {
          "fixedAmount": 10,
          "variablePercentage": 100
        },
        "additionalCommission": {
          "fixedAmount": 10,
          "variablePercentage": 50,
          "balanceAccountId": "BA3227C223222H5HQ2XX77VVH"
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-split-configuration-profile-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|
|body|body|[SplitConfiguration](#schemasplitconfiguration)|false|none|
|» description|body|string|true|Your description for the split configuration.|
|» rules|body|[[SplitConfigurationRule](#schemasplitconfigurationrule)]|true|Array of rules that define the split configuration behavior.|

> Example responses

```json
  "description": "Your description for the split configuration",

      "currency": "ANY",
```

## Create a rule

<a id="opIdpost-merchants-merchantId-splitConfigurations-splitConfigurationId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/splitConfigurations/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "paymentMethod": "visa",
    "shopperInteraction": "POS",
    "fundingSource": "ANY",
    "currency": "USD",
    "splitLogic": {
      "paymentFee": "deductFromLiableAccount",
      "chargeback": "deductFromLiableAccount",
      "tip": "addToOneBalanceAccount",
      "remainder": "addToLiableAccount",
      "commission": {
        "fixedAmount": 10,
        "variablePercentage": 100
      },
      "additionalCommission": {
        "fixedAmount": 10,
        "variablePercentage": 50,
        "balanceAccountId": "BA3227C223222H5HQ2XX77VVH"
      }
    }
  }'
```

`POST /merchants/{merchantId}/splitConfigurations/{splitConfigurationId}`

[Creates a rule](https://docs.adyen.com/platforms/automatic-split-configuration/manage-split-configurations/api/#create-rule) in the split configuration profile specified in the path.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API - SplitConfiguration read and write

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "paymentMethod": "visa",
  "shopperInteraction": "POS",
  "fundingSource": "ANY",
  "currency": "USD",
  "splitLogic": {
    "paymentFee": "deductFromLiableAccount",
    "chargeback": "deductFromLiableAccount",
    "tip": "addToOneBalanceAccount",
    "remainder": "addToLiableAccount",
    "commission": {
      "fixedAmount": 10,
      "variablePercentage": 100
    },
    "additionalCommission": {
      "fixedAmount": 10,
      "variablePercentage": 50,
      "balanceAccountId": "BA3227C223222H5HQ2XX77VVH"
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-rule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|
|splitConfigurationId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the split configuration.|
|body|body|[SplitConfigurationRule](#schemasplitconfigurationrule)|false|none|
|» cardRegion|body|string|false|The card region condition that determines whether the [split logic](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/Management/latest/post/merchants/(merchantId)/splitConfigurations#request-rules-splitLogic) applies to the transaction.<br><br>Possible values:<br>* **domestic**: The card issuer and the store where the transaction is processed are registered in the same country.<br>* **international**: The card issuer and the store where the transaction is processed are registered in different countries or regions. Includes all **interRegional** and **intraRegional** transactions.<br>* **interRegional**: The card issuer and the store where the transaction is processed are registered in different regions.<br>* **intraRegional**: The card issuer and the store where the transaction is processed are registered in different countries, but in the same region.<br>* **intraEEA**: The card issuer and the store where the transaction is processed are registered in different countries, but in the European Economic Area (EEA).<br>* **ANY**: Applies to all transactions, regardless of the processing and issuing country/region.|
|» cardUsageType|body|string|false|The card usage type condition that determines whether the split logic applies to commercial cards, consumer cards, or all cards.<br><br>* **ANY** (default): The split logic applies to all cards, regardless of its usage type.<br>* **commercial**: The split logic applies to commercial cards only.<br>* **consumer**: The split logic applies to consumer cards only.|
|» currency|body|string|true|The currency condition that defines whether the split logic applies.<br>Its value must be a three-character [ISO currency code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217).|
|» fundingSource|body|string|true|The funding source of the payment method.<br><br>Possible values:<br>* **credit**<br>* **debit**<br>* **prepaid**<br>* **deferred_debit**<br>* **charged**<br>* **ANY**|
|» paymentMethod|body|string|true|The payment method condition that defines whether the split logic applies.<br><br>Possible values:<br>* [Payment method variant](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/paymentmethodvariant): Apply the split logic for a specific payment method.<br>* **ANY**: Apply the split logic for all available payment methods.|
|» shopperInteraction|body|string|true|The sales channel condition that defines whether the split logic applies.<br><br>Possible values:<br>* **Ecommerce**: Online transactions where the cardholder is present.<br>* **ContAuth**: Card on file and/or subscription transactions, where the cardholder is known to the merchant (returning customer).<br>* **Moto**: Mail-order and telephone-order transactions where the customer is in contact with the merchant via email or telephone.<br>* **POS**: Point-of-sale transactions where the customer is physically present to make a payment using a secure payment terminal.<br>* **ANY**: All sales channels.|
|» splitLogic|body|[SplitConfigurationLogic](#schemasplitconfigurationlogic)|true|Contains the split logic that is applied if the rule conditions are met.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» cardRegion|international|
|» cardRegion|intraEEA|
|» cardRegion|intraRegional|
|» cardRegion|interRegional|
|» cardRegion|domestic|
|» cardRegion|ANY|
|» cardUsageType|commercial|
|» cardUsageType|consumer|
|» cardUsageType|ANY|
|» fundingSource|charged|
|» fundingSource|credit|
|» fundingSource|debit|
|» fundingSource|deferred_debit|
|» fundingSource|prepaid|
|» fundingSource|ANY|
|» shopperInteraction|Ecommerce|
|» shopperInteraction|ContAuth|
|» shopperInteraction|Moto|
|» shopperInteraction|POS|
|» shopperInteraction|ANY|

> Example responses

## Update the split conditions

<a id="opIdpatch-merchants-merchantId-splitConfigurations-splitConfigurationId-rules-ruleId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/splitConfigurations/string/rules/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "currency": "EUR",
    "fundingSource": "ANY",
    "paymentMethod": "visa",
    "shopperInteraction": "ANY"
  }'
```

`PATCH /merchants/{merchantId}/splitConfigurations/{splitConfigurationId}/rules/{ruleId}`

Changes the [split conditions of the rule](https://docs.adyen.com/platforms/automatic-split-configuration/manage-split-configurations/api/#update-condition) specified in the path.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API - SplitConfiguration read and write

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "currency": "EUR",
  "fundingSource": "ANY",
  "paymentMethod": "visa",
  "shopperInteraction": "ANY"
}
```

<h3 id="update-the-split-conditions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|
|splitConfigurationId|path|string|true|The identifier of the split configuration.|
|ruleId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the split configuration rule.|
|body|body|[UpdateSplitConfigurationRuleRequest](#schemaupdatesplitconfigurationrulerequest)|false|none|
|» cardUsageType|body|string|false|The card usage type condition that determines whether the split logic applies to commercial cards, consumer cards, or all cards.<br><br>* **ANY** (default): The split logic applies to all cards, regardless of its usage type.<br>* **commercial**: The split logic applies to commercial cards only.<br>* **consumer**: The split logic applies to consumer cards only.|
|» currency|body|string|true|The currency condition that defines whether the split logic applies.<br>Its value must be a three-character [ISO currency code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217).|
|» fundingSource|body|string|true|The funding source of the payment method.<br><br>Possible values:<br>* **credit**<br>* **debit**<br>* **prepaid**<br>* **deferred_debit**<br>* **charged**<br>* **ANY**|
|» paymentMethod|body|string|true|The payment method condition that defines whether the split logic applies.<br><br>Possible values:<br>* [Payment method variant](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/paymentmethodvariant): Apply the split logic for a specific payment method.<br>* **ANY**: Apply the split logic for all available payment methods.|
|» shopperInteraction|body|string|true|The sales channel condition that defines whether the split logic applies.<br><br>Possible values:<br>* **Ecommerce**: Online transactions where the cardholder is present.<br>* **ContAuth**: Card on file and/or subscription transactions, where the cardholder is known to the merchant (returning customer).<br>* **Moto**: Mail-order and telephone-order transactions where the customer is in contact with the merchant via email or telephone.<br>* **POS**: Point-of-sale transactions where the customer is physically present to make a payment using a secure payment terminal.<br>* **ANY**: All sales channels.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» cardUsageType|commercial|
|» cardUsageType|consumer|
|» cardUsageType|ANY|

## Update the split logic

<a id="opIdpatch-merchants-merchantId-splitConfigurations-splitConfigurationId-rules-ruleId-splitLogic-splitLogicId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/splitConfigurations/string/rules/string/splitLogic/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "additionalCommission": {
      "fixedAmount": 100,
      "variablePercentage": 0,
      "balanceAccountId": "BA3227C223222H5HQ2XX77VVH"
    },
    "chargeback": "deductFromLiableAccount",
    "commission": {
      "fixedAmount": 100,
      "variablePercentage": 100
    },
    "paymentFee": "deductFromLiableAccount",
    "remainder": "addToLiableAccount",
    "tip": "addToLiableAccount"
  }'
```

`PATCH /merchants/{merchantId}/splitConfigurations/{splitConfigurationId}/rules/{ruleId}/splitLogic/{splitLogicId}`

Changes the [split logic](https://docs.adyen.com/platforms/automatic-split-configuration/manage-split-configurations/api/#update-split-logic) specified in the path.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API - SplitConfiguration read and write

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "additionalCommission": {
    "fixedAmount": 100,
    "variablePercentage": 0,
    "balanceAccountId": "BA3227C223222H5HQ2XX77VVH"
  },
  "chargeback": "deductFromLiableAccount",
  "commission": {
    "fixedAmount": 100,
    "variablePercentage": 100
  },
  "paymentFee": "deductFromLiableAccount",
  "remainder": "addToLiableAccount",
  "tip": "addToLiableAccount"
}
```

<h3 id="update-the-split-logic-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|
|splitConfigurationId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the split configuration.|
|ruleId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the split configuration rule.|
|splitLogicId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the split configuration split.|
|body|body|[UpdateSplitConfigurationLogicRequest](#schemaupdatesplitconfigurationlogicrequest)|false|none|
|» acquiringFees|body|string|false|Deducts the acquiring fees (the aggregated amount of interchange and scheme fee) from the specified balance account.<br><br>Possible values: **deductFromLiableAccount**, **deductFromOneBalanceAccount**.|
|» additionalCommission|body|[AdditionalCommission](#schemaadditionalcommission)|false|Defines whether to book an additional commission for payments to your user's balance account. The commission amount can be defined as a fixed amount (specified in minor units), a percentage (specified in basis points), or both.|
|» adyenCommission|body|string|false|Deducts the transaction fee due to Adyen under [blended rates](https://www.adyen.com/knowledge-hub/guides/payments-training-guide/get-the-best-from-your-card-processing) from the specified balance account.<br><br>Possible values: **deductFromLiableAccount**, **deductFromOneBalanceAccount**.|
|» adyenFees|body|string|false|Deducts the fees due to Adyen (markup or commission) from the specified balance account.<br><br>Possible values: **deductFromLiableAccount**, **deductFromOneBalanceAccount**.|
|» adyenMarkup|body|string|false|Deducts the transaction fee due to Adyen under [Interchange ++ pricing](https://www.adyen.com/what-is-interchange) from the specified balance account.<br><br>Possible values: **deductFromLiableAccount**, **deductFromOneBalanceAccount**.|
|» chargeback|body|string|false|Specifies how and from which balance account(s) to deduct the chargeback amount.<br><br>Possible values: **deductFromLiableAccount**, **deductFromOneBalanceAccount**, **deductAccordingToSplitRatio**.|
|» chargebackCostAllocation|body|string|false|Deducts the chargeback costs from the specified balance account.<br><br>Possible values: **deductFromLiableAccount**, **deductFromOneBalanceAccount**|
|» commission|body|[Commission](#schemacommission)|true|Defines your platform's commission for the processed payments as a fixed amount (specified in minor units), a percentage (specified in basis points), or both. The commission is booked to your platform's liable balance account.|
|» dcc|body|[SplitDcc](#schemasplitdcc)|false|Defines the logic for booking the markup paid by the customer for Dynamic Currency Conversion (DCC).<br><br>> This field is in pilot phase, and not yet available for all platforms.|
|» interchange|body|string|false|Deducts the interchange fee from specified balance account.<br><br>Possible values: **deductFromLiableAccount**, **deductFromOneBalanceAccount**.|
|» paymentFee|body|string|false|Deducts all transaction fees incurred by the payment from the specified balance account. The transaction fees include the acquiring fees (interchange and scheme fee), and the fees due to Adyen (markup or commission). You can book any and all these fees to different balance account by specifying other transaction fee parameters in your split configuration profile:<br><br>- [`adyenCommission`](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/Management/latest/post/merchants/(merchantId)/splitConfigurations#request-rules-splitLogic-adyenCommission): The transaction fee due to Adyen under [blended rates](https://www.adyen.com/knowledge-hub/interchange-fees-explained#interchange-vs-blended).<br>- [`adyenMarkup`](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/Management/latest/post/merchants/(merchantId)/splitConfigurations#request-rules-splitLogic-adyenMarkup): The transaction fee due to Adyen under [Interchange ++ pricing](https://www.adyen.com/knowledge-hub/interchange-fees-explained#interchange-vs-blended).<br>- [`schemeFee`](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/Management/latest/post/merchants/(merchantId)/splitConfigurations#request-rules-splitLogic-schemeFee): The fee paid to the card scheme for using their network.<br>- [`interchange`](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/Management/latest/post/merchants/(merchantId)/splitConfigurations#request-rules-splitLogic-interchange): The fee paid to the issuer for each payment transaction made with the card network.<br>- [`adyenFees`](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/Management/latest/post/merchants/(merchantId)/splitConfigurations#request-rules-splitLogic-adyenFees): The aggregated amount of Adyen's commission and markup.<br>- [`acquiringFees`](https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/Management/latest/post/merchants/(merchantId)/splitConfigurations#request-rules-splitLogic-acquiringFees): The aggregated amount of the interchange and scheme fees.<br><br>If you don't include at least one transaction fee type in the `splitLogic` object, Adyen updates the payment request with the `paymentFee` parameter, booking all transaction fees to your platform's liable balance account.<br><br>Possible values: **deductFromLiableAccount**, **deductFromOneBalanceAccount**.|
|» refund|body|string|false|Specifies how and from which balance account(s) to deduct the refund amount.<br><br>Possible values: **deductFromLiableAccount**, **deductFromOneBalanceAccount**, **deductAccordingToSplitRatio**|
|» refundCostAllocation|body|string|false|Deducts the refund costs from the specified balance account.<br><br>Possible values: **deductFromLiableAccount**, **deductFromOneBalanceAccount**|
|» remainder|body|string|false|Books the amount left over after currency conversion to the specified balance account.<br><br>Possible values: **addToLiableAccount**, **addToOneBalanceAccount**.|
|» schemeFee|body|string|false|Deducts the scheme fee from the specified balance account.<br><br>Possible values: **deductFromLiableAccount**, **deductFromOneBalanceAccount**.|
|» surcharge|body|string|false|Books the surcharge amount to the specified balance account.<br><br>Possible values: **addToLiableAccount**, **addToOneBalanceAccount**|
|» tip|body|string|false|Books the tips (gratuity) to the specified balance account.<br><br>Possible values: **addToLiableAccount**, **addToOneBalanceAccount**.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» acquiringFees|deductFromLiableAccount|
|» acquiringFees|deductFromOneBalanceAccount|
|» adyenCommission|deductFromLiableAccount|
|» adyenCommission|deductFromOneBalanceAccount|
|» adyenFees|deductFromLiableAccount|
|» adyenFees|deductFromOneBalanceAccount|
|» adyenMarkup|deductFromLiableAccount|
|» adyenMarkup|deductFromOneBalanceAccount|
|» chargeback|deductFromLiableAccount|
|» chargeback|deductFromOneBalanceAccount|
|» chargeback|deductAccordingToSplitRatio|
|» chargebackCostAllocation|deductFromLiableAccount|
|» chargebackCostAllocation|deductFromOneBalanceAccount|
|» interchange|deductFromLiableAccount|
|» interchange|deductFromOneBalanceAccount|
|» paymentFee|deductFromLiableAccount|
|» paymentFee|deductFromOneBalanceAccount|
|» refund|deductFromLiableAccount|
|» refund|deductFromOneBalanceAccount|
|» refund|deductAccordingToSplitRatio|
|» refundCostAllocation|deductFromLiableAccount|
|» refundCostAllocation|deductFromOneBalanceAccount|
|» remainder|addToLiableAccount|
|» remainder|addToOneBalanceAccount|
|» schemeFee|deductFromLiableAccount|
|» schemeFee|deductFromOneBalanceAccount|
|» surcharge|addToLiableAccount|
|» surcharge|addToOneBalanceAccount|
|» tip|addToLiableAccount|
|» tip|addToOneBalanceAccount|

```json
  "description": "Your description for the split configuration",
  "rules": [
    {
      "currency": "ANY",
      "fundingSource": "ANY",
      "paymentMethod": "ANY",
      "ruleId": "SCRL4224P22322585HPCX384JW65VW",
      "shopperInteraction": "ANY",

        "additionalCommission": {
          "fixedAmount": 10,
```

## Generate a client certificate

<a id="opIdpost-companies-companyId-clientCertificates"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/string/clientCertificates \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "apiCredential": "ws_356950@Company.TestCompany",
    "certificateSigningRequest": ""
  }'
```

`POST /companies/{companyId}/clientCertificates`

Generates a client certificate for secure communication with Adyen using mutual TLS (mTLS). Provide a certificate signing request (CSR). Adyen signs it and returns the client certificate.

The CSR must be generated by a key pair that meets the following criteria:
* Key ownership: the CSR must be signed by the associated private key.
* Key type: RSA with a minimum key size of 2048 bits, or ECC with a minimum key size of 224 bits.

A company account can have a maximum of 10 valid client certificates at a time.

The subject distinguished name (`subjectDN`) of the issued certificate is constructed by Adyen from the path `companyId` and the request `apiCredential`. The subject in your CSR is not used. The returned `subjectDN` has the format `UID={apiCredential}-Company.{companyId},CN={apiCredential}-Company.{companyId},O=Company.{companyId}`.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API - Client certificates read and write


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "apiCredential": "ws_356950@Company.TestCompany",
  "certificateSigningRequest": ""
}
```

<h3 id="generate-a-client-certificate-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|companyId|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[ClientCertificateRequest](#schemaclientcertificaterequest)|true|Certificate signing request details.|
|» apiCredential|body|string|true|The API Credential that you want to use this certificate with, in the format 'ws_*@Company.*'.<br>NOTE: You must assign the DN on that specified API credential with the one from the generated client certificate. Accomplish this either through the Customer Area API Credential page or the PATCH endpoint for apiCredentials<br>|
|» certificateSigningRequest|body|string|true|Certificate signing request. Must be a Base64-encoded DER string. Only the public key is enrolled; see the enroll operation for subject handling.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "caChain": [
    "",
    ""
  ],
  "id": "CC_28C8D8EA0BA0303D793FD392ECF9D09ED865C6E",
  "leaf": "",
  "serialNumber": "28C8D8EA0BA0303D793FD392ECF9D09ED865C6E",
  "subjectDN": "UID=ws_356950@Company.TestCompany-Company.TestCompany,CN=ws_356950@Company.TestCompany-Company.TestCompany,O=Company.TestCompany"
}
```

`POST /companies/{companyId}/campaignManagement`

Creates a new donation campaign, to give shoppers the option to donate to a nonprofit organization when making a payment. A campaign can be for online payments, in-person payments, or both online and in-person payments.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Campaign Management read and write

## Get the donation campaigns for an account holder

<a id="opIdget-companies-companyId-campaignManagement-accountHolders-accountHolderId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/string/campaignManagement/accountHolders/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /companies/{companyId}/campaignManagement/accountHolders/{accountHolderId}`

Returns a paginated list of donation campaigns associated with the account holder specified in the path. You can filter the list by campaign status.

To make this request, your API credential must have one of the following [roles](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Campaign Management read
* Management API—Campaign Management read and write

<h3 id="get-the-donation-campaigns-for-an-account-holder-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|companyId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the company account.|
|accountHolderId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the account holder.|
|status|query|string|false|The campaign status to return campaigns that match. Allowed values: **inactive**, **active**, or **ended**.|
|pageNumber|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of the page to fetch.|
|pageSize|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of items to have on a page, maximum 100. The default is 10 items on a page.|

<a id="opIdpatch-companies-companyId-campaignManagement-donationCampaignId"></a>


`PATCH /companies/{companyId}/campaignManagement/{donationCampaignId}`

Updates the properties of the donation campaign specified in the path. Note the following restrictions: 

* You cannot use a PATCH request to update the campaign status. To activate or end a campaign, make a POST request to the `/campaignManagement/{campaignId}/status/{status}` endpoint.
* You get a validation error if you add account holders that are not compatible with the nonprofit.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Campaign Management read and write

> Body parameter

```json
    ]
  }
}
```

## Activate or end a donation campaign

<a id="opIdpost-companies-companyId-campaignManagement-donationCampaignId-status-status"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/string/campaignManagement/string/status/activate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /companies/{companyId}/campaignManagement/{donationCampaignId}/status/{status}`

Starts or stops the donation campaign specified in the path, by providing a path parameter. 
Use the path parameter **activate** to start an inactive campaign, or **end** to stop an active campaign. Other status transitions are not allowed.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#api-permissions):
* Management API—Campaign Management read and write

<h3 id="activate-or-end-a-donation-campaign-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|companyId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the company account.|
|donationCampaignId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the donation campaign to activate or end.|
|status|path|[CampaignStatusTransition](#schemacampaignstatustransition)|true|The desired status change. Possible values: **activate** or **end**.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|activate|
|status|end|

## Get a list of nonprofits

<a id="opIdpost-companies-companyId-nonprofits"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/string/nonprofits \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "accountHolderIds": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /companies/{companyId}/nonprofits`

Returns a list of supported nonprofit organizations to choose from when creating a donation campaign. The list only contains nonprofits that are compatible with all the account holders specified in the request.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "accountHolderIds": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="get-a-list-of-nonprofits-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|companyId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the company account.|
|searchTerm|query|string|false|A query to return nonprofit organizations for, maximum 100 characters. For example, `&searchTerm=clean%20water`.|
|pageNumber|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of the page to fetch.|
|pageSize|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of items to have on a page, maximum 100. The default is 10 items on a page.|
|goal|query|[string]|false|One or more United Nations Sustainable Development Goals to return nonprofit organizations for. Format: `unsdg_<number>`, for example, `&goal=unsdg_6&goal=unsdg_2`.|
|body|body|[ListNonprofitsRequest](#schemalistnonprofitsrequest)|false|none|
|» accountHolderIds|body|[string]|true|The unique identifiers of the account holders to be included in a donation campaign.|

> Example responses

```json
    },
```

<h1 id="management-api-terminal-themes---company-level">Terminal themes - company level</h1>

## List terminal themes

<a id="opIdget-companies-companyId-terminalThemes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/string/terminalThemes \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /companies/{companyId}/terminalThemes`

Returns a paginated list of terminal themes for the company specified in the path and all the associated merchant accounts. The response provides only the metadata of the themes. Assets (images and videos) are not included. To obtain the URLs for the assets of a specific theme, make a GET request to the `/companies/{companyId}/terminalThemes/{id}` endpoint.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#manage-api-permissions): 
- Management API - Terminal themes read and write

<h3 id="list-terminal-themes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|companyId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the company account.|
|pageSize|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of themes to return per page. If not specified, the list has 10 themes per page.|
|page|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of the page to fetch. If not specified, the list starts from page 1.|
|search|query|string|false|A search term to filter themes by name. The match is case-insensitive and returns any theme with a name that contains the search term.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "THEM_001ABC",
      "name": "BrandDark",
      "mode": "dark"
    },

      "name": "BrandLight",
      "mode": "light"
    }
  ],
  "hasNextPage": false
}
```

## Create a terminal theme

<a id="opIdpost-companies-companyId-terminalThemes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/string/terminalThemes \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "MyBrandTheme",
    "mode": "dark"
  }'
```

`POST /companies/{companyId}/terminalThemes`

Creates a terminal theme for the company specified in the path, to customize screens shown on Android payment terminals. This request only creates a basic theme with a name and a dark or light mode. We refer to this as the metadata of the theme. 

Next steps are to add terminal model-specific assets (images or videos) to the theme, and to apply (activate) the theme. 

The theme name must be unique for the company account; other accounts can have a theme with the same name. 

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#manage-api-permissions):
- Management API - Terminal themes read and write

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "MyBrandTheme",
  "mode": "dark"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-terminal-theme-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|companyId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the company account.|
|body|body|[CreateThemeRequest](#schemacreatethemerequest)|true|The theme to create.|
|» mode|body|[ThemeMode](#schemathememode)|true|The terminal display mode. Possible values: **dark** for a dark screen background, or **light** for a light screen background.|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the theme. Must be unique within the account specified in the path. Maximum 255 characters.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» mode|dark|
|» mode|light|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "id": "THEM_001ABC",
  "name": "MyBrandTheme",
  "mode": "dark"
}
```

## Unapply a terminal theme

<a id="opIdpost-companies-companyId-terminalThemes-unapply"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/string/terminalThemes/unapply \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /companies/{companyId}/terminalThemes/unapply`

Resets the theme assignment for the company specified in the path. The terminals under this company will switch to the default Adyen theme. However, if a custom theme is applied at a lower level (merchant account, store, or individual terminal) those terminals continue to use their current theme.

The theme itself remains unchanged and is not deleted. 

If no custom theme is currently applied to the company, this request returns a **200 OK** response without error. 

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#manage-api-permissions): 
- Management API - Terminal themes read and write

<h3 id="unapply-a-terminal-theme-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|companyId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the company account.|

> Example responses

```json
  "status": "success"
}
```

## Add an asset to a terminal theme

<a id="opIdpost-companies-companyId-terminalThemes-id-assets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/companies/string/terminalThemes/string/assets?type=logo&model=All' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file'
```

`POST /companies/{companyId}/terminalThemes/{id}/assets`

Adds an image or video (an 'asset') to a terminal theme owned by the company specified in the path. This endpoint is [rate limited](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

An asset is used for a specific screen type or screen element, and a specific Android terminal model. You must specify this using the query parameters `type` and `model`. The asset binary itself is uploaded as multipart/form-data with a single file part called `file`, which must declare one of the following supported Content-Type values:

- **image/svg+xml**: only for the combination `type` **logo** with `model` **All**.
- **video/mp4** or **video/quicktime**: only for `model` **SFO1** or **M450**.
- **image/jpeg** (or **image/jpg**): for all `model` values except **All**.
- **image/png**: for all `model` values except **All**.
- **image/gif**: for all `model` values except **SFO1** and **M450**.

The maximum size of the asset depends on the terminal model: 100 MB for `model` **SFO1** and **M450**, or 10 MB for all other `model` values.

If the theme already has an asset for the same combination of `type` and `model`, the request fails and you need to upload the new asset using the `/companies/{companyId}/terminalThemes/{id}/assets/replace` endpoint.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#manage-api-permissions): 
- Management API - Terminal themes read and write

> Body parameter

```yaml
file: string
```

<h3 id="add-an-asset-to-a-terminal-theme-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|companyId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the company account.|
|id|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the terminal theme.|
|type|query|string|true|The screen type or screen element that the asset is for:<br><br>- **logo**: your logo. Only supported if `model` is **All**.<br>- **homeScreen**: the default background screen.<br>- **idleScreen**: a screensaver shown when the terminal is inactive. Only supported if `model` is **SFO1** or **M450**.<br>- **afterPaymentScreen**: a screen shown after the payment is completed.<br>- **shopperEngagementScreen**: a screen shown during a [shopper engagement](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/shopper-engagement) request. Only supported if `model` is **SFO1** or **M450**.|
|model|query|string|true|The Android terminal model that the asset is for. Use **All** only if the `type` is **logo**. For every other screen type specify a single Android terminal model such as **AMS1**.|
|body|body|[AssetUploadRequest](#schemaassetuploadrequest)|true|The asset file.|
|» file|body|string(binary)|true|The asset file. The part must declare a specific supported Content-Type; which Content-Type is accepted depends on the asset `type` and terminal `model` (see the endpoint description for the full mapping). The file extension is derived from it. A request with a generic or missing Content-Type such as application/octet-stream is rejected with response code **422**. The maximum asset size depends on the terminal model: up to 100 MB for SFO1 and M450, or 10 MB for all other models.|

|type|shopperEngagementScreen|

|model|S1E4Pro|
|model|S1U2|
|model|S1U2M4|
|model|LDN1|
|model|AMS1|
|model|P630|

`DELETE /companies/{companyId}/terminalThemes/{id}/assets`

## List terminal themes

<a id="opIdget-merchants-merchantId-terminalThemes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/terminalThemes \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /merchants/{merchantId}/terminalThemes`

Returns a paginated list of terminal themes for the merchant account specified in the path. The response provides only the metadata of the themes. Assets (images and videos) are not included. To get the URLs for the assets of a specific theme, make a GET request to the `/merchants/{merchantId}/terminalThemes/{id}` endpoint 

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#manage-api-permissions): 
- Management API - Terminal themes read and write

<h3 id="list-terminal-themes-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|
|pageSize|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of themes to return per page. If not specified, the list has 10 themes per page.|
|page|query|integer(int32)|false|The number of the page to fetch. If not specified, the list starts from page 1.|
|search|query|string|false|A search term to filter themes by name. The match is case-insensitive and returns any theme with a name that contains the search term.|

## Create a terminal theme

<a id="opIdpost-merchants-merchantId-terminalThemes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/terminalThemes \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "MyBrandTheme",
    "mode": "dark"
  }'
```

`POST /merchants/{merchantId}/terminalThemes`

Creates a terminal theme for the merchant account specified in the path, to customize screens shown on Android payment terminals. This request only creates a basic theme with a name and a dark or light mode. We refer to this as the metadata of the theme. 

Next steps are to add terminal model-specific assets (images or videos) to the theme, and to apply (activate) the theme. 

The theme name must be unique for the merchant account; other accounts can have a theme with the same name. 

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#manage-api-permissions):
- Management API - Terminal themes read and write

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "MyBrandTheme",
  "mode": "dark"
}
```

|body|body|[CreateThemeRequest](#schemacreatethemerequest)|true|The theme to create.|
|» mode|body|[ThemeMode](#schemathememode)|true|The terminal display mode. Possible values: **dark** for a dark screen background, or **light** for a light screen background.|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the theme. Must be unique within the account specified in the path. Maximum 255 characters.|

|» mode|light|

## Unapply a terminal theme

<a id="opIdpost-merchants-merchantId-terminalThemes-unapply"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/terminalThemes/unapply \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /merchants/{merchantId}/terminalThemes/unapply`

Resets the theme assignment for the merchant account specified in the path. The Android terminals under this merchant account will switch to the custom theme applied at the company level, or to the default Adyen theme if there is no custom theme applied at the company level. However, if a custom theme is applied at a lower level (store or individual terminal) those terminals continue to use their current theme.

The theme itself remains unchanged and is not deleted. 

If no custom theme is currently applied to the merchant account, this request returns a **200 OK** response without error. 

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#manage-api-permissions): 
- Management API - Terminal themes read and write

## Add an asset to a terminal theme

<a id="opIdpost-merchants-merchantId-terminalThemes-id-assets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/terminalThemes/string/assets?type=logo&model=All' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file'
```

`POST /merchants/{merchantId}/terminalThemes/{id}/assets`

Adds an image or video (an 'asset') to a terminal theme owned by the merchant account specified in the path. This endpoint is [rate limited](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).

An asset is used for a specific screen type or screen element, and a specific Android terminal model. You must specify this using the query parameters `type` and `model`. The asset binary itself is uploaded as multipart/form-data with a single file part called `file`, which must declare one of the following supported Content-Type values:

- **image/svg+xml**: only for the combination `type` **logo** with `model` **All**.
- **video/mp4** or **video/quicktime**: only for `model` **SFO1** or **M450**.
- **image/jpeg** (or **image/jpg**): for all `model` values except **All**.
- **image/png**: for all `model` values except **All**.
- **image/gif**: for all `model` values except **SFO1** and **M450**.

The maximum size of the asset depends on the terminal model: 100 MB for `model` **SFO1** and **M450**, or 10 MB for all other `model` values.

If the theme already has an asset for the same combination of `type` and `model`, the request fails and you need to upload the new asset using the `/merchants/{merchantId}/terminalThemes/{id}/assets/replace` endpoint.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#manage-api-permissions): 
- Management API - Terminal themes read and write

> Body parameter

```yaml
file: string
```

<h3 id="add-an-asset-to-a-terminal-theme-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|
|id|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the terminal theme.|
|type|query|string|true|The screen type or screen element that the asset is for:<br><br>- **logo**: your logo. Only supported if `model` is **All**.<br>- **homeScreen**: the default background screen.<br>- **idleScreen**: a screensaver shown when the terminal is inactive. Only supported if `model` is **SFO1** or **M450**.<br>- **afterPaymentScreen**: a screen shown after the payment is completed.<br>- **shopperEngagementScreen**: a screen shown during a [shopper engagement](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/shopper-engagement) request. Only supported if `model` is **SFO1** or **M450**.|
|model|query|string|true|The Android terminal model that the asset is for. Use **All** only if the `type` is **logo**. For every other screen type specify a single Android terminal model such as **AMS1**.|
|body|body|[AssetUploadRequest](#schemaassetuploadrequest)|true|The asset file.|
|» file|body|string(binary)|true|The asset file. The part must declare a specific supported Content-Type; which Content-Type is accepted depends on the asset `type` and terminal `model` (see the endpoint description for the full mapping). The file extension is derived from it. A request with a generic or missing Content-Type such as application/octet-stream is rejected with response code **422**. The maximum asset size depends on the terminal model: up to 100 MB for SFO1 and M450, or 10 MB for all other models.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|type|logo|
|type|homeScreen|
|type|idleScreen|
|type|afterPaymentScreen|
|type|shopperEngagementScreen|
|model|All|
|model|SFO1|
|model|M450|
|model|S1F2|
|model|S1E2L|
|model|S1F2L|
|model|S1F4Pro|

## Delete an asset from a terminal theme

<a id="opIddelete-merchants-merchantId-terminalThemes-id-assets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/terminalThemes/string/assets?type=logo&model=All' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /merchants/{merchantId}/terminalThemes/{id}/assets`

Deletes a single asset from a terminal theme owned by the merchant account specified in the path. To identify the asset you want to remove, you must use the query parameters `type` and `model`.

When the `type` is **logo**, deleting the asset is blocked if the theme owner is not allowed to edit logos. 

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#manage-api-permissions): 
- Management API - Terminal themes read and write

|id|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the terminal theme.|
|type|query|string|true|The screen type or screen element that the asset is for:<br><br>- **logo**: your logo. Only supported if `model` is **All**.<br>- **homeScreen**: the default background screen.<br>- **idleScreen**: a screensaver shown when the terminal is inactive. Only supported if `model` is **SFO1** or **M450**.<br>- **afterPaymentScreen**: a screen shown after the payment is completed.<br>- **shopperEngagementScreen**: a screen shown during [shopper engagement](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/shopper-engagement) requests. Only supported if `model` is **SFO1** or **M450**.|
|model|query|string|true|The Android terminal model that the asset is for. Use **All** only if the `type` is **logo**. For every other screen type specify a single Android terminal model such as **AMS1**.|

## Replace a theme asset

<a id="opIdpost-merchants-merchantId-terminalThemes-id-assets-replace"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/merchants/string/terminalThemes/string/assets/replace?type=logo&model=All' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file'
```

`POST /merchants/{merchantId}/terminalThemes/{id}/assets/replace`

Replaces an existing image or video (an 'asset') of a terminal theme owned by the merchant account specified in the path. This endpoint is [rate limited](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/automating-terminal-management#rate-limits-in-the-live-environment).\n\n"
An asset is used for a specific screen type or screen element, and a specific Android 
terminal model. You must specify this using the query parameters `type` and `model`. 
The asset binary itself is uploaded as multipart/form-data with a single file part 
called `file`, which must declare one of the following supported Content-Type values:

- **image/svg+xml**: only for the combination `type` **logo** with `model` **All**.
- **video/mp4** or **video/quicktime**: only for `model` **SFO1** or **M450**.
- **image/jpeg** (or **image/jpg**): for all `model` values except **All**.
- **image/png**: for all `model` values except **All**.
- **image/gif**: for all `model` values except **SFO1** and **M450**.
The maximum size of the asset depends on the terminal model: 100 MB for `model` **SFO1** 
and **M450**, or 10 MB for all other `model` values.

You can upload an asset using this endpoint if the theme already has an asset with the specified combination of `type` and `model`. If that is not the case, the request fails and you need to use the endpoint `/merchants/{merchantId}/terminalThemes/{id}/assets` instead.

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#manage-api-permissions): 
- Management API - Terminal themes read and write

> Body parameter

```yaml
file: string
```

<h3 id="replace-a-theme-asset-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|merchantId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the merchant account.|
|id|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the terminal theme.|
|type|query|string|true|The screen type or screen element that the asset is for:<br><br>- **logo**: your logo. Only supported if `model` is **All**.<br>- **homeScreen**: the default background screen.<br>- **idleScreen**: a screensaver shown when the terminal is inactive. Only supported if `model` is **SFO1** or **M450**.<br>- **afterPaymentScreen**: a screen shown after the payment is completed.<br>- **shopperEngagementScreen**: a screen shown during [shopper engagement](https://docs.adyen.com/point-of-sale/shopper-engagement) requests. Only supported if `model` is **SFO1** or **M450**.|
|model|query|string|true|The Android terminal model that the asset is for. Use **All** only if the `type` is **logo**. For every other screen type specify a single Android terminal model such as **AMS1**.|
|body|body|[AssetUploadRequest](#schemaassetuploadrequest)|true|The asset file.|
|» file|body|string(binary)|true|The asset file. The part must declare a specific supported Content-Type; which Content-Type is accepted depends on the asset `type` and terminal `model` (see the endpoint description for the full mapping). The file extension is derived from it. A request with a generic or missing Content-Type such as application/octet-stream is rejected with response code **422**. The maximum asset size depends on the terminal model: up to 100 MB for SFO1 and M450, or 10 MB for all other models.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|type|logo|
|type|homeScreen|
|type|idleScreen|
|type|afterPaymentScreen|
|type|shopperEngagementScreen|
|model|All|
|model|SFO1|
|model|M450|
|model|S1F2|
|model|S1E2L|
|model|S1F2L|
|model|S1F4Pro|
|model|S1E4Pro|
|model|S1U2|
|model|S1U2M4|
|model|LDN1|
|model|AMS1|
|model|P630|

## Unapply a terminal theme

<a id="opIdpost-stores-storeId-terminalThemes-unapply"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://management-test.adyen.com/v3/stores/string/terminalThemes/unapply \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /stores/{storeId}/terminalThemes/unapply`

Resets the theme assignment for the store specified in the path. The Android terminals under this store will switch to the theme from the next higher level where a custom theme is applied (merchant account or company) or the default Adyen theme. However, if a custom theme is applied to individual terminals, those terminals continue to use their current theme.

The theme itself remains unchanged and is not deleted. 

If no custom theme is currently applied to the store, this request returns a **200 OK** response without error. 

To make this request, your API credential must have the following [role](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/api-credentials#manage-api-permissions):
- Management API - Terminal themes read and write

<h3 id="unapply-a-terminal-theme-2-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|storeId|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the store.|


> 404 Response

```json
{
  "type": "https://docs.adyen.com/errors/not-found",
  "title": "Not Found",
  "detail": "Account not found or not accessible",
  "requestId": "f7a3b2c1d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5",
  "status": 404,
  "errorCode": "00_404"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "type": "https://docs.adyen.com/errors/validation",
  "title": "Unprocessable Entity",
  "detail": "To apply or unapply a theme the terminal must be deployed or boarded",
  "requestId": "d42c493b5176df89e51516c6060cc34c",
  "status": 422,
  "errorCode": "00_422"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "type": "https://docs.adyen.com/errors/internal-server-error",
  "title": "Internal Server Error",
  "status": 500,
  "errorCode": "00_500"
}
```

<h3 id="apply-a-terminal-theme-3-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Unprocessable Entity|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal Server Error|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
BasicAuth, ApiKeyAuth
</aside>

```json
    }
```

```json
  "filterMerchantAccounts": [
    "string"
  ],

  "type": "string",

}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|acceptsExpiredCertificate|boolean|false|none|Indicates if expired SSL certificates are accepted. Default value: **false**.|
|acceptsSelfSignedCertificate|boolean|false|none|Indicates if self-signed SSL certificates are accepted. Default value: **false**.|
|acceptsUntrustedRootCertificate|boolean|false|none|Indicates if untrusted SSL certificates are accepted. Default value: **false**.|
|active|boolean|true|none|Indicates if the webhook configuration is active. The field must be **true** for us to send webhooks about events related an account.|
|additionalSettings|[AdditionalSettings](#schemaadditionalsettings)|false|none|Additional shopper and transaction information to be included in your [standard webhooks](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/webhooks/webhook-types/#event-codes). Find out more about the available [additional settings](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/webhooks/additional-settings).|
|communicationFormat|string|true|none|Format or protocol for receiving webhooks. Possible values:<br>* **soap**<br>* **http**<br>* **json** |
|description|string|false|none|Your description for this webhook configuration.|
|encryptionProtocol|string|false|none|SSL version to access the public webhook URL specified in the `url` field. Possible values:<br>* **TLSv1.3**<br>* **TLSv1.2**<br>* **HTTP** - Only allowed on Test environment.<br><br>If not specified, the webhook will use `sslVersion`: **TLSv1.2**.|
|filterMerchantAccountType|string|true|none|Shows how merchant accounts are filtered when configuring the webhook. <br><br>Possible values:<br>*  **allAccounts** : Includes all merchant accounts, and does not require specifying `filterMerchantAccounts`.<br>*  **includeAccounts** : The webhook is configured for the merchant accounts listed in `filterMerchantAccounts`.<br>*  **excludeAccounts** : The webhook is not configured for the merchant accounts listed in `filterMerchantAccounts`.<br><br>|
|filterMerchantAccounts|[string]|true|none|A list of merchant account names that are included or excluded from receiving the webhook. Inclusion or exclusion is based on the value defined for `filterMerchantAccountType`.<br><br>Required if `filterMerchantAccountType` is either:<br>* **includeAccounts**<br>* **excludeAccounts**<br><br>Not needed for `filterMerchantAccountType`: **allAccounts**.|
|networkType|string|false|none|Network type for Terminal API notification webhooks. Possible values:<br>* **public**<br>* **local**<br><br>Default Value: **public**.|
|password|string|false|none|Password to access the webhook URL.|
|populateSoapActionHeader|boolean|false|none|Indicates if the SOAP action header needs to be populated. Default value: **false**.<br><br>Only applies if `communicationFormat`: **soap**.|
|type|string|true|none|The type of webhook that is being created. Possible values are:<br><br>- **standard**<br>- **account-settings-notification**<br>- **banktransfer-notification**<br>- **boletobancario-notification**<br>- **directdebit-notification**<br>- **ach-notification-of-change-notification**<br>- **direct-debit-notice-of-change-notification**<br>- **pending-notification**<br>- **ideal-notification**<br>- **ideal-pending-notification**<br>- **report-notification**<br>- **rreq-notification**<br>- **terminal-settings**<br>- **terminal-boarding**<br><br>Find out more about [standard webhooks](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/webhooks/webhook-types/#event-codes) and [other types of webhooks](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/webhooks/webhook-types/#other-webhooks).|
|url|string|true|none|Public URL where webhooks will be sent, for example **https://www.domain.com/webhook-endpoint**.|
|username|string|false|none|Username to access the webhook URL.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|communicationFormat|http|
|communicationFormat|json|
|communicationFormat|soap|
|encryptionProtocol|HTTP|
|encryptionProtocol|TLSv1.2|
|encryptionProtocol|TLSv1.3|
|filterMerchantAccountType|allAccounts|
|filterMerchantAccountType|excludeAccounts|
|filterMerchantAccountType|includeAccounts|
|networkType|local|
|networkType|public|
